shlokas.meaning: Those who make Me their refuge, who strive for liberation from decay and Death, they realise the Supreme Spirit, which is their own real Self, and in which all action finds its consummation.

shlokas.name: Shloka 30
shlokas.interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of complete knowledge of Krishna, including His manifestations in the material world (adhibhuta), His divine form (adhidaiva), and His presence in sacrifices (adhiyajna). It suggests that those who possess this comprehensive understanding can maintain their focus on Krishna even at the time of death, ensuring spiritual liberation.
shlokas.life_application: This verse encourages individuals to cultivate a deep, all-encompassing understanding of the Divine in various aspects of life. By recognizing the presence of the Supreme in material elements, celestial beings, and sacred rituals, one can develop a constant awareness of the Divine. This practice helps in maintaining spiritual focus during challenging times, especially when facing death, leading to peace of mind and spiritual progress. It teaches us to integrate spiritual awareness into our daily lives, seeing the Divine in all aspects of existence.

chapters.name: Aksara Brahma Yoga
chapters.summary: Chapter 8 of the Bhagavad Gita, known as Aksara Brahma Yoga, focuses on the nature of the Ultimate Reality (Brahman) and the process of attaining it. Krishna explains the concepts of Brahman, Adhyatma, Karma, Adhibhuta, Adhidaiva, and Adhiyajna. He emphasizes the importance of remembering the Divine at the time of death and describes the paths of light and darkness that souls take after death.
chapters.main_theme: The importance of constant remembrance of the Divine, especially at the time of death, and the process of attaining liberation

chapters.philosophical_progression: The chapter begins with Arjuna's questions about fundamental spiritual concepts. Krishna then explains the nature of Ultimate Reality, emphasizing the importance of divine remembrance, especially at the time of death. The discussion progresses to cosmic time scales and cycles of creation and dissolution, highlighting the vastness of existence. Krishna then describes the different paths souls take after death, concluding with the superiority of yoga and spiritual knowledge over ritualistic practices.
chapters.chapter_relevance: Chapter 8 is crucial in the Bhagavad Gita as it delves into the nature of Ultimate Reality and the process of attaining it. It addresses fundamental questions about existence, the self, and the divine, while emphasizing the importance of constant divine remembrance. The chapter provides a comprehensive view of cosmic cycles, the paths of liberation, and the significance of one's state of consciousness at the time of death. It serves as a bridge between the more practical teachings of earlier chapters and the deeper metaphysical discussions that follow.

shlokas.name: Shloka 1
shlokas.interpretation: This verse marks the beginning of Chapter 8, where Arjuna seeks clarification on several fundamental concepts of spiritual knowledge. His questions demonstrate a deep curiosity about the nature of existence, the self, and the divine. By addressing Krishna as 'Purushottama' (Supreme Person), Arjuna acknowledges Krishna's divine status and his ability to provide authoritative answers to these profound inquiries.
shlokas.life_application: This verse encourages us to cultivate a spirit of inquiry and seek deeper understanding of life's fundamental questions. In our daily lives, we can apply this teaching by regularly reflecting on our existence, actions, and relationship with the divine. By questioning and seeking answers about our true nature and purpose, we can gain clarity and make more conscious decisions aligned with our spiritual goals.

shlokas.name: Shloka 2
shlokas.interpretation: This verse raises two profound questions about the nature of the Divine and its relationship to the individual soul. Arjuna seeks to understand the concept of Adhiyajna (the Lord of all sacrifices) and how it relates to the physical body. He also inquires about how self-controlled individuals can remember the Divine at the time of death. These questions delve into the core of spiritual practice and the ultimate goal of union with the Divine.
shlokas.life_application: This verse encourages us to cultivate a constant awareness of the Divine presence in our lives, not just in moments of worship but in our everyday existence. It teaches us to live with the end in mind, preparing ourselves spiritually for the ultimate transition. By developing self-control and steadfast devotion, we can face life's challenges and uncertainties with greater equanimity. This approach can help in reducing anxiety about death and fostering a more meaningful and purposeful life.

shlokas.name: Shloka 3
shlokas.interpretation: This verse delves into the fundamental concepts of Brahman, Adhyatma, and Karma. It emphasizes the eternal nature of Brahman as the supreme reality, introduces the concept of individual nature (Svabhava) as the essence of the self, and explains Karma as the creative force behind the manifestation of beings. This shloka provides a concise yet profound explanation of the cosmic order and individual existence within it.
shlokas.life_application: Understanding this verse can help individuals recognize their true nature beyond the physical body, encouraging spiritual growth. It promotes self-reflection on one's inherent qualities (Svabhava) and mindfulness of how actions (Karma) shape one's life and future. This knowledge can lead to more conscious decision-making, reduced attachment to material outcomes, and a greater sense of purpose aligned with one's spiritual essence.

commentaries.madhvacharya: ।।परममक्षरं ब्रह्म। वेदादिशङ्काव्यावृत्त्यर्थमेतत्। आत्मन्यधि यत्तदध्यात्मम्। आत्माधिकारे यत्तदिति वा। तथा हि -- जैवः स्वभावः। स्वाख्यो भावः स्वभाव इति व्युत्पत्त्या जीवो वा स्वभावः सर्वदा अस्त्येव एकप्रकारेणेति भावः। अन्तःकरणादिव्यावृत्त्यर्थो भावशब्दः। न ह्येकप्रकारेण स्थितिरन्तःकरणादेः विकारित्वात्। स्वशब्द ईश्वरव्यावृत्त्यर्थः। भूतानां जीवानां भावानां जडपदार्थानां चोद्भवकरीश्वरक्रिया विसर्गः विशेषेण सर्जनं विसर्ग इत्यर्थः।

śrī bhagavānuvāca
akṣaraṅ brahma paramaṅ svabhāvō.dhyātmamucyatē.
bhūtabhāvōdbhavakarō visargaḥ karmasaṅjñitaḥ
shlokas.meaning: The Lord Shri Krishna replied: The Supreme Spirit is the Highest Imperishable Self, and Its Nature is spiritual consciousness. The worlds have been created and are supported by an emanation from the Spirit which is called the Law.

shlokas.name: Shloka 4
shlokas.interpretation: This verse explains the different aspects of the manifest world and their relationship to the Supreme. It introduces the concepts of Adhibhuta (physical manifestation), Adhidaiva (the controlling deities), and Adhiyajna (the Supreme Lord as the overseer of all sacrifices). Krishna reveals that He is present in every living being as the Supersoul, overseeing all actions and sacrifices.
shlokas.life_application: Understanding this verse helps one recognize the temporary nature of the physical world and the eternal presence of the Divine in all beings. It encourages individuals to look beyond material attachments and cultivate a deeper spiritual awareness. This knowledge can lead to a more balanced approach to life, where one performs their duties as a form of sacrifice to the Divine, fostering inner peace and harmony with the cosmic order.

translation.purohitSwami: Matter consists of the forms that perish; Divinity is the Supreme Self; and He who inspires the spirit of sacrifice in man, O noblest of thy race, is I Myself, Who now stand in human form before thee.

commentaries.madhvacharya: ।।भूतानि सशरीरान् जीवानधिकृत्य यत्तदधिभूतम्। क्षरो भावो विनाशिकार्यपदार्थः। अव्यक्तान्तर्भावेऽपि तस्याप्यन्यथाभावाख्यो विनाशोऽस्त्येव। तच्चोक्तम् -- अव्यक्तं परमे व्योम्नि निष्क्रिये सम्प्रलीयते इति।तस्मादव्यक्तमुत्पन्नं त्रिगुणं द्विजसत्तम इति च।विकारोऽव्यक्तजन्म हि इति च स्कान्दे। पुरि शयनात्पुरुषो जीवः स च सङ्कर्षणो ब्रह्मा वा। स सर्वदेवानधिकृत्य तत्पतिरित्यधिदैवतम् देवाधिकारस्थ इति वा।सर्वयज्ञभोक्तृत्वादेरधियज्ञः। अन्योऽधियज्ञोऽग्न्यादिः प्रसिद्ध इति देह इति विशेषणम्।भोक्तारं यज्ञतपसां [5।29]।त्रैविद्या मां [9।20]।ये त्वन्यदेवताभक्ताः। [9।23] एतस्य वा अक्षरस्य प्रशासने ৷৷. गार्गि ददतो मनुष्याः प्रशंसन्ति यजमानं देवाः [बृ.उ.3।8।9] इत्यादेः।कुतो ह्यस्य ध्रुवः स्वर्गः कुतो नैश्श्रेयसं पदम् [मं.भा.12।334।2] इत्यादिपरिहारश्च मोक्षधर्मे। भगवांश्चेत्तद्भोक्तृत्वादेरधियज्ञत्वं सिद्धमिति  कथमित्यस्य परिहारः पृथङ्नोक्तः। सर्वप्राणिदेहस्थरूपेण साधियज्ञः।अत्रेति स्वदेहनिवृत्त्यर्थम्। न हि तत्रेश्वरस्य नियन्तृत्वं पृथगस्ति। नात्रोक्तं ब्रह्म भगवतोऽन्यत्।ते ब्रह्म [7।29] इत्युक्त्वासाधिभूताधिदैवं मां साधियज्ञं च ये विदुः [7।30] इति परामर्शात् तस्यैव च प्रश्नात्।साधियज्ञं इति भेदप्रतीतेस्तन्निवृत्त्यर्थंअधियज्ञोऽहं  इत्युक्तम्। मामित्यभेदप्रसिद्धेरक्षरमित्येवोक्तम्। आह च गीताकल्पे -- देहस्थविष्णुरूपाणि अधियज्ञ इतीरितः। कर्मेश्वरस्य सृष्ट्यर्थं तच्चापीच्छाद्यमुच्यते। अधिभूतं जडं प्रोक्तमध्यात्मं जीव उच्यते। हिरण्यगर्भोऽधिदैवं देवः सङ्कर्षणोऽपि वा। ब्रह्म नारायणो देवः सर्वदेवेश्वरेश्वरः इति।यथा प्रतीतं वा सर्वमत्र नैव विरुध्यते इति। स्कान्दे च -- आत्माभिमानाधिकारस्थितमध्यात्ममुच्यते। देहाद्बाह्यं विनाऽतीव बाह्यत्वादधिदैवतम्। देवाधिकारगं सर्वं महाभूताधिकारगम्। तत्कारणं तथा कार्यमधिभूतं तदन्तिकात् इति। महाकौर्मे च -- अध्यात्मं देहपर्यन्तं केवलात्मोपकारकम्। सदेहजीवभूतानि यत्तेषामुपकारकृत्। अधिभूतं तु मायान्तं देवानामधिदैवतम् इति।
commentaries.ramanujacharya:
।।ऐश्वर्यार्थिनां ज्ञातव्यतया निर्दिष्टम्
अधिभूतं क्षरो भावः
वियदादिभूतेषु वर्तमानः तत्परिणामविशेषः क्षरणस्वभावो विलक्षणः शब्दस्पर्शादिः साश्रयः विलक्षणाः साश्रयाः शब्दस्पर्शरूपरसगन्धाः ऐश्वर्यार्थिभिः प्राप्याः तैः अनुसंधेयाः।
पुरुषश्च अधिदैवतम्
अधिदैवतशब्दनिर्दिष्टः पुरुषः अधिदैवतं दैवतोपरि वर्तमानम् इन्द्रप्रजापतिप्रभृतिकृत्स्नदैवतोपरि वर्तमानः इन्द्रप्रजापतिप्रभृतीनां भोग्यजाताद् विलक्षणशब्दादेः भोक्ता पुरुषः सा च भोक्तृत्वावस्था ऐश्वर्यार्थिभिः प्राप्यतया अनुसन्धेया।
अधियज्ञः अहम् एव
अधियज्ञशब्दनिर्दिष्टो अहम् एव अधियज्ञः यज्ञैः आराध्यतया वर्तमानः अत्रेन्द्रादौ मम देहभूते आत्मतया अवस्थितः अहम् एव यज्ञैः आराध्य इति महायज्ञादिनित्यनैमित्तकानुष्ठानवेलायां त्रयाणाम् अधिकारिणाम् अनुसन्धेयम् एतत्।इदमपि त्रयाणां साधारणम् --

shlokas.meaning: Matter consists of the forms that perish; Divinity is the Supreme Self; and He who inspires the spirit of sacrifice in man, O noblest of thy race, is I Myself, Who now stand in human form before thee.

shlokas.name: Shloka 5
shlokas.interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of one's final thoughts at the time of death. It suggests that if a person remembers Krishna (the Supreme Being) at the moment of leaving their body, they will attain His divine state. This teaching underscores the power of devotion and the significance of maintaining spiritual consciousness throughout life, as our last thoughts are often a reflection of our deepest attachments and most ingrained habits.
shlokas.life_application: This verse encourages individuals to cultivate a consistent spiritual practice and devotion throughout their lives. It teaches that by regularly remembering and connecting with the divine, one can develop the habit of maintaining spiritual consciousness even in challenging times. This practice can help in facing death with calmness and clarity, and also in dealing with daily stresses and anxieties by maintaining a higher perspective. It emphasizes the importance of living mindfully and purposefully, always being aware of one's ultimate spiritual goal.

shlokas.meaning: Whosoever at the time of death thinks only of Me, and thinking thus leaves the body and goes forth, assuredly he will know Me.

shlokas.name: Shloka 6
shlokas.interpretation: This verse emphasizes the power of one's final thoughts at the moment of death. It suggests that our predominant thoughts and attachments throughout life shape our consciousness at death, which in turn influences our next birth or spiritual destination. This teaching underscores the importance of cultivating positive, spiritual thoughts and detachment from worldly desires throughout one's life.
shlokas.life_application: This verse encourages individuals to live mindfully and cultivate positive thoughts and spiritual practices consistently. It can be applied to overcome fear of death by focusing on spiritual growth, practicing meditation, and maintaining a positive mindset. In daily life, it motivates one to be conscious of their thoughts and actions, knowing that these shape their character and future. It also emphasizes the importance of staying focused on one's goals and aspirations, as persistent thoughts and efforts lead to their realization.

shlokas.name: Shloka 7
shlokas.interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of constant remembrance of the Divine while performing one's duties. It suggests that by maintaining a continuous connection with the Supreme Being, even amidst life's challenges and battles, one can achieve ultimate union with the Divine. The verse also highlights the concept of surrender, indicating that when one's mind and intellect are fully devoted to the Divine, the path to spiritual realization becomes clear and certain.
shlokas.life_application: This teaching can be applied in daily life by maintaining awareness of a higher purpose or spiritual goal while engaging in work or facing challenges. It encourages individuals to cultivate a practice of mindfulness, where they remain connected to their spiritual center even during mundane activities. This approach can help in reducing stress, improving focus, and finding meaning in all aspects of life. By surrendering the ego and aligning one's thoughts and actions with higher principles, a person can navigate life's complexities with greater clarity and purpose.

shlokas.name: Shloka 8
shlokas.interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of consistent spiritual practice (abhyasa yoga) and unwavering focus on the Divine. It suggests that through regular meditation and by keeping one's mind fixed on the Supreme Being, one can attain the highest spiritual realization. The verse highlights the power of devoted thought and the transformative nature of consistent spiritual discipline.
shlokas.life_application: This teaching can be applied to achieve success in any endeavor by emphasizing the power of focused practice and unwavering dedication. In daily life, it encourages developing a routine of mindfulness or meditation, setting clear goals, and maintaining consistent effort towards them. It also teaches the importance of avoiding distractions and maintaining a singular focus on one's chosen path or objective, whether in career, relationships, or personal growth.

shlokas.name: Shloka 9
shlokas.interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of meditating on the Supreme Being's transcendental nature. It describes the Divine as the omniscient poet, the primeval, the controller, subtler than the subtlest, the sustainer of all, inconceivable in form, self-luminous, and beyond all darkness of ignorance. The verse encourages seekers to constantly remember these qualities of the Divine to attain spiritual realization.
shlokas.life_application: This verse can be applied in daily life to cultivate a deeper spiritual practice and perspective. By regularly contemplating the divine attributes mentioned, one can develop humility, expand consciousness, and find inner peace. It encourages individuals to look beyond the material world and seek a higher understanding of existence, which can help in overcoming ego, reducing stress, and finding purpose in life. The practice of remembering these qualities can also serve as a form of meditation, improving focus and mental clarity in various life situations.

shlokas.name: Shloka 10
shlokas.interpretation: This verse describes the process of leaving the body at the time of death for an advanced yogi. It emphasizes the importance of unwavering focus, devotion, and yogic practices in achieving union with the Supreme Divine Being. The verse highlights the significance of controlling one's life force (prana) and directing it to the space between the eyebrows, a practice known as samadhi in yoga.
shlokas.life_application: This verse teaches us the importance of maintaining focus and devotion in our spiritual practices, especially during challenging times. It encourages developing mental strength through yoga and meditation, which can help in facing life's difficulties with calmness and clarity. The practice of controlling one's breath and focusing the mind can be applied in daily life to reduce stress, improve concentration, and achieve a sense of inner peace. It also reminds us to live with awareness and purpose, as our state of mind at critical moments can significantly impact our life's journey.

commentaries.madhvacharya: ।।वायुजयादियोगयुक्तानां मृतिकाले कर्तव्यमाह विशेषतः -- प्रयाणकाल इति। वायुजयादिरहितानामपि ज्ञानभक्तिवैराग्यादिसम्पूर्णानां भवत्येव मुक्तिः। तद्वतां त्वीषज्ज्ञानाद्यसम्पूर्णनामपि निपुणानां तद्बलात्कथञ्चिद्भवतीति विशेषः। उक्तं च भागवते [3।5।4546।]पानेन ते देव कथासुधायाः प्रवृद्धभक्त्या विशदाशया ये। वैराग्यसारं प्रतिलभ्य बोधं यथाऽञ्जसा त्वापुरकुण्ठधिष्ण्यम्। तथाऽपरे त्वात्मसमाधियोगबलेन जित्वा प्रकृतिं बलिष्ठाम्। त्वामेव धीराः पुरुषं विशन्ति तेषां श्रमः स्यान्न तु सेवया ते इति।ये तु तद्भाविता लोका (केह्ये) एकान्तित्वं समाश्रिताः। एतदभ्यधिकं तेषां तत्तेजः प्रविशन्त्युत [मा.भा.12।334।44] इति च मोक्षधर्मे।सम्पूर्णानां भवेन्मोक्षो विरक्तिज्ञानभक्तिभिः। नियमेन तथापीरजयादियुतयोगिनाम्। वश्यत्वान्मनसस्त्वीषत्पूर्वमप्याप्यते ध्रुवम् इति च व्यासयोगे।

shlokas.name: Shloka 11
shlokas.interpretation: This verse introduces the concept of the Supreme Absolute Truth, or Brahman, as the ultimate goal of spiritual seekers. It emphasizes the importance of Vedic knowledge, renunciation, and celibacy in attaining this highest state. The verse also highlights that this supreme state is beyond the material world and can be reached through dedicated spiritual practice and detachment from worldly desires.
shlokas.life_application: This verse encourages individuals to pursue higher knowledge and spiritual growth. It teaches that by cultivating discipline, practicing detachment from material desires, and focusing on spiritual studies, one can overcome life's challenges and find true purpose. This approach can help in managing stress, improving self-control, and developing a more balanced and fulfilling life perspective.

shlokas.name: Shloka 12
shlokas.interpretation: This verse describes the process of yogic meditation and the control of life force for achieving union with the Divine. It emphasizes the importance of sensory withdrawal, mental concentration, and the regulation of vital energy (prana) in spiritual practice. The verse suggests that by mastering these techniques, one can attain a state of deep meditation and ultimately, liberation.
shlokas.life_application: This verse can be applied in daily life to manage stress, improve focus, and enhance overall well-being. By practicing sensory control and mindfulness, one can reduce distractions and increase productivity. The breathing techniques mentioned can be used for relaxation and anxiety management. Regular meditation as described can lead to better emotional regulation, clearer thinking, and a more balanced approach to life's challenges.

shlokas.name: Shloka 13
shlokas.interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of remembering the Divine at the time of death. It suggests that by uttering the sacred syllable 'Om' and meditating on the Supreme Being while leaving the body, one can attain the highest spiritual destination. The verse highlights the power of focused consciousness and devotion at the final moment of life, indicating that one's last thoughts can significantly influence their spiritual journey after death.
shlokas.life_application: This teaching can be applied to cultivate a constant awareness of the Divine in daily life, not just at the time of death. It encourages individuals to practice mindfulness, meditation, and devotion regularly, so that remembering the Divine becomes second nature. This practice can help in reducing fear of death, maintaining calm in difficult situations, and living a more purposeful and spiritually aligned life. It also emphasizes the importance of maintaining positive and elevating thoughts, as our mental state significantly influences our experiences and outcomes.

shlokas.name: Shloka 14
shlokas.interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of unwavering devotion and constant remembrance of the Divine. It suggests that spiritual realization is not about complex rituals or practices, but about maintaining a continuous connection with the Supreme. The verse also implies that God is easily accessible to those who are sincerely devoted, breaking down the notion of God being distant or difficult to reach.
shlokas.life_application: This teaching can be applied in daily life by encouraging individuals to maintain focus on their goals or spiritual practices amidst distractions. It promotes the idea that consistency and dedication in any endeavor, be it personal, professional, or spiritual, leads to success. The verse also offers solace to those feeling distant from their spiritual path, assuring them that sincere effort and constant mindfulness can bridge any perceived gap.

shlokas.name: Shloka 15
shlokas.interpretation: This verse emphasizes the ultimate goal of spiritual practice in Hinduism - liberation from the cycle of birth and death. It suggests that those who attain the highest realization by reaching Krishna do not have to return to the material world, which is characterized by impermanence and suffering. The verse implies that true spiritual perfection leads to a permanent state of bliss and freedom from worldly afflictions.
shlokas.life_application: This verse encourages individuals to pursue spiritual growth and self-realization as the ultimate solution to life's problems. It teaches that by focusing on spiritual practices, cultivating devotion, and striving for union with the Divine, one can overcome the cycle of suffering and attain lasting peace. In practical terms, this can motivate people to prioritize inner development over material pursuits, practice detachment from temporary pleasures, and seek meaning beyond worldly achievements.

नाप्नुवन्ति महात्मानः संसिद्धिं परमां गताः
shlokas.transliteration:
māmupētya punarjanma duḥkhālayamaśāśvatam.
nāpnuvanti mahātmānaḥ saṅsiddhiṅ paramāṅ gatāḥ
shlokas.meaning: Coming thus unto Me, these great souls go no more to the misery and death of earthly life, for they have gained perfection.

shlokas.name: Shloka 16
shlokas.interpretation: This verse highlights the cyclical nature of existence within the material universe and contrasts it with the permanent liberation achieved by reaching Krishna. It emphasizes the impermanence of even the highest material realms and the supreme goal of attaining Krishna's eternal abode.
shlokas.life_application: This verse encourages individuals to seek spiritual growth and ultimate liberation rather than temporary material pleasures. It can motivate people to focus on long-term spiritual goals, practice detachment from worldly pursuits, and cultivate devotion to the Divine. This teaching can help in overcoming fear of death, finding purpose in life, and maintaining equanimity in the face of life's ups and downs.

scripts.devanagari:
आब्रह्मभुवनाल्लोकाः पुनरावर्तिनोऽर्जुन।
मामुपेत्य तु कौन्तेय पुनर्जन्म न विद्यते
scripts.roman:
ābrahmabhuvanāllōkāḥ punarāvartinō.rjuna.
māmupētya tu kauntēya punarjanma na vidyatē
scripts.kannada:
ಆಬ್ರಹ್ಮಭುವನಾಲ್ಲೋಕಾಃ ಪುನರಾವರ್ತಿನೋರ್ಜುನ.
ಮಾಮುಪೇತ್ಯ ತು ಕೌನ್ತೇಯ ಪುನರ್ಜನ್ಮ ನ ವಿದ್ಯತೇ
scripts.telugu:
ఆబ్రహ్మభువనాల్లోకాః పునరావర్తినోర్జున.
మాముపేత్య తు కౌన్తేయ పునర్జన్మ న విద్యతే

translation.purohitSwami: The worlds, with the whole realm of creation, come and go; but, O Arjuna, whoso comes to Me, for him there is nor rebirth.

commentaries.madhvacharya: ।।महामेरुस्थब्रह्मसदनमारभ्य न पुनरावृत्तिः। तच्चोक्तं नारायणगोपालकल्पेआ मेरुब्रह्मसदनादा जनान्न जनिर्भुवि। तथाप्यभावः सर्वत्र प्राप्यैव वसुदेवजम् इति।

shlokas.name: Shloka 17
shlokas.interpretation: This verse introduces the concept of cosmic time scales, specifically Brahma's day and night. It emphasizes the vast difference between human perception of time and the cosmic reality. The verse suggests that our understanding of existence and the universe is limited, and there are greater cycles of creation and dissolution beyond our immediate comprehension.
shlokas.life_application: This verse encourages us to broaden our perspective and think beyond our limited lifespan. It can help in dealing with immediate problems by reminding us of the vastness of existence, potentially reducing anxiety about short-term issues. It also promotes humility by highlighting the limitations of human understanding, encouraging continuous learning and spiritual growth.

scripts.devanagari:
सहस्रयुगपर्यन्तमहर्यद्ब्रह्मणो विदुः।
रात्रिं युगसहस्रान्तां तेऽहोरात्रविदो जनाः
scripts.roman:
sahasrayugaparyantamaharyadbrahmaṇō viduḥ.
rātriṅ yugasahasrāntāṅ tē.hōrātravidō janāḥ
scripts.kannada:
ಸಹಸ್ರಯುಗಪರ್ಯನ್ತಮಹರ್ಯದ್ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಣೋ ವಿದುಃ.
ರಾತ್ರಿಂ ಯುಗಸಹಸ್ರಾನ್ತಾಂ ತೇಹೋರಾತ್ರವಿದೋ ಜನಾಃ
scripts.telugu:
సహస్రయుగపర్యన్తమహర్యద్బ్రహ్మణో విదుః.
రాత్రిం యుగసహస్రాన్తాం తేహోరాత్రవిదో జనాః

translation.purohitSwami: Those who understand the cosmic day and cosmic night know that one day of creation is a thousand cycles, and that the night is of equal length.

commentaries.shankaracharya:
।। --,

चतुर्मुखस्य

shlokas.meaning: Those who understand the cosmic day and cosmic night know that one day of creation is a thousand cycles, and that the night is of equal length.

shlokas.name: Shloka 18
shlokas.interpretation: This verse describes the cosmic cycle of creation and dissolution, emphasizing the eternal nature of existence. It illustrates how all manifested beings emerge from the unmanifest at the beginning of Brahma's day and dissolve back into the unmanifest at the onset of Brahma's night. This cycle represents the continuous process of evolution and involution in the universe, highlighting the impermanence of the manifest world and the eternal nature of the unmanifest.
shlokas.life_application: This verse can help individuals understand the transient nature of life and material possessions, encouraging detachment and acceptance of change. It teaches us to focus on the eternal, unchanging aspects of existence rather than temporary manifestations. This perspective can reduce anxiety about loss and change, promoting inner peace and resilience in facing life's ups and downs. It also inspires a broader, more cosmic view of existence, helping to put personal problems into perspective.

scripts.devanagari:
अव्यक्ताद्व्यक्तयः सर्वाः प्रभवन्त्यहरागमे।
रात्र्यागमे प्रलीयन्ते तत्रैवाव्यक्तसंज्ञके
scripts.roman:
avyaktādvyaktayaḥ sarvāḥ prabhavantyaharāgamē.
rātryāgamē pralīyantē tatraivāvyaktasaṅjñakē
scripts.kannada:
ಅವ್ಯಕ್ತಾದ್ವ್ಯಕ್ತಯಃ ಸರ್ವಾಃ ಪ್ರಭವನ್ತ್ಯಹರಾಗಮೇ.
ರಾತ್ರ್ಯಾಗಮೇ ಪ್ರಲೀಯನ್ತೇ ತತ್ರೈವಾವ್ಯಕ್ತಸಂಜ್ಞಕೇ
scripts.telugu:
అవ్యక్తాద్వ్యక్తయః సర్వాః ప్రభవన్త్యహరాగమే.
రాత్ర్యాగమే ప్రలీయన్తే తత్రైవావ్యక్తసంజ్ఞకే

translation.purohitSwami: At the dawning of that day all objects in manifestation stream forth from the Unmanifest, and when evening falls they are dissolved into It again.

shlokas.name: Shloka 19
shlokas.interpretation: This verse describes the cyclical nature of creation and dissolution in the universe. It emphasizes the concept of cosmic time and the impermanence of all material manifestations. The verse suggests that all beings are subject to the cosmic cycle of creation and destruction, which is beyond their control. This cycle is likened to the coming of day and night, symbolizing the eternal nature of existence and non-existence.
shlokas.life_application: This verse can help individuals understand the transient nature of life and material possessions, encouraging detachment and acceptance of change. It can be applied to overcome fear of death, reduce attachment to worldly things, and develop a broader perspective on personal struggles. The teaching can also inspire people to make the most of their current existence while understanding that all things are part of a greater cosmic cycle.

scripts.devanagari:
भूतग्रामः स एवायं भूत्वा भूत्वा प्रलीयते।
रात्र्यागमेऽवशः पार्थ प्रभवत्यहरागमे

bhūtagrāmaḥ sa ēvāyaṅ bhūtvā bhūtvā pralīyatē.

రాత్ర్యాగమేవశః పార్థ ప్రభవత్యహరాగమే

translation.purohitSwami: The same multitude of beings, which have lived on earth so often, all are dissolved as the night of the universe approaches, to issue forth anew when morning breaks. Thus is it ordained.

shlokas.meaning: The same multitude of beings, which have lived on earth so often, all are dissolved as the night of the universe approaches, to issue forth anew when morning breaks. Thus is it ordained.

shlokas.name: Shloka 20
shlokas.interpretation: This verse introduces the concept of the Supreme Eternal Reality that exists beyond the manifest and unmanifest states of material nature. It emphasizes the indestructible and eternal nature of the Supreme Being, which remains unaffected even when all other beings and forms in the universe are destroyed. This shloka points to the transcendental nature of the Ultimate Reality, which is beyond the cycle of creation and destruction that governs the material world.
shlokas.life_application: Understanding this verse can help individuals develop a broader perspective on life and death. It encourages seeking a connection with the eternal, unchanging reality beyond the temporary material world. This knowledge can provide solace during times of loss or change, fostering resilience and inner peace. It also motivates spiritual seekers to look beyond the apparent reality and explore their true, eternal nature, potentially leading to reduced attachment to material possessions and increased focus on spiritual growth.

shlokas.name: Shloka 21
shlokas.interpretation: This verse describes the ultimate destination of the soul, which is the Supreme Abode of the Divine. It emphasizes the eternal and imperishable nature of this realm, which is beyond human perception and understanding. The verse suggests that once a soul reaches this state, it achieves liberation from the cycle of birth and death, attaining eternal union with the Divine.
shlokas.life_application: This verse encourages individuals to focus on spiritual growth and self-realization, reminding them of the ultimate goal of human existence. It can motivate people to look beyond material pursuits and temporary pleasures, inspiring them to cultivate virtues and practices that lead to spiritual evolution. In daily life, it can help in developing detachment from worldly outcomes and fostering a sense of inner peace and purpose.

shlokas.name: Shloka 22
shlokas.interpretation: This verse emphasizes the supreme importance of devotion (bhakti) in realizing the Supreme Being. It suggests that the Ultimate Reality, which pervades all existence, can only be attained through unwavering and exclusive devotion. The shloka presents a holistic view of the Divine, describing it as both immanent (present within all beings) and transcendent (pervading everything).
shlokas.life_application: This verse encourages individuals to cultivate single-minded devotion to achieve spiritual realization. It teaches that by recognizing the divine presence in all things, one can develop a more compassionate and unified worldview. This understanding can help in overcoming ego, reducing conflicts, and fostering a sense of interconnectedness with all beings, leading to a more harmonious and purposeful life.

shlokas.name: Shloka 23
shlokas.interpretation: This verse introduces the concept of different paths that yogis take after death, specifically referring to the timing of departure and its consequences. It emphasizes the importance of the moment of death in determining one's spiritual journey and suggests that there are specific times that lead to either liberation or rebirth. The verse also highlights Krishna's role as a teacher, preparing to impart crucial knowledge about these paths to Arjuna.
shlokas.life_application: This verse encourages individuals to live mindfully and spiritually at all times, as the moment of death is unpredictable. It teaches the importance of constant spiritual practice and maintaining awareness of the divine, so that one is prepared for the final moment. In daily life, this can translate to making conscious choices, living ethically, and cultivating a spiritual mindset to ensure that one's actions align with higher spiritual goals, regardless of when death may occur.

shlokas.name: Shloka 24
shlokas.interpretation: This verse describes the path of light, also known as the Devayana or the path of the gods. It outlines the auspicious time and conditions under which enlightened souls depart from this world to attain Brahman, the Ultimate Reality. The verse emphasizes the importance of the timing of death in relation to cosmic cycles and suggests that those who have realized Brahman follow this path to ultimate liberation.
shlokas.life_application: This verse encourages individuals to pursue spiritual knowledge and self-realization throughout their lives, rather than waiting for a specific time. It emphasizes the importance of constant spiritual practice and awareness, as one cannot predict the time of death. The teaching can motivate people to live righteously, cultivate wisdom, and maintain a positive mindset, preparing themselves for the ultimate journey at any moment.

shlokas.name: Shloka 25
shlokas.interpretation: This verse describes the path of gradual liberation known as the 'path of smoke' or 'path of darkness'. It represents a less direct route to spiritual realization, associated with worldly achievements and temporary heavenly pleasures. The verse suggests that yogis who depart during these less auspicious times return to the cycle of rebirth, implying the importance of timing and consciousness at the moment of death in determining one's spiritual journey.
shlokas.life_application: This verse encourages us to remain spiritually vigilant at all times, as the moment of death is uncertain. It teaches the importance of continuous spiritual practice and maintaining a higher state of consciousness. In daily life, it reminds us to make the most of our time, focusing on spiritual growth alongside worldly duties, and to approach our actions with awareness of their long-term spiritual consequences.

shlokas.name: Shloka 26
shlokas.interpretation: This verse describes the two paths of departure from the material world: the bright path (śukla gati) and the dark path (kṛṣṇa gati). The bright path leads to liberation and non-return, while the dark path results in rebirth. It emphasizes the importance of one's state of consciousness and actions at the time of death, as they determine the soul's journey after leaving the body.
shlokas.life_application: This verse encourages individuals to live a life of spiritual awareness and righteous action. It teaches us to make conscious choices that align with higher spiritual goals, as these decisions impact our future beyond this lifetime. In daily life, it reminds us to cultivate positive thoughts, perform selfless actions, and maintain spiritual practices, as these lead to higher consciousness and ultimately to liberation from the cycle of birth and death.

shlokas.name: Shloka 27
shlokas.interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of spiritual knowledge and yoga practice. It suggests that a true yogi, armed with the understanding of the two paths (light and darkness), is never deluded. The verse encourages constant engagement in yoga, implying that spiritual awareness and practice lead to clarity and liberation from confusion in all circumstances.
shlokas.life_application: This verse can be applied in daily life by encouraging individuals to cultivate spiritual awareness and maintain a consistent practice of self-reflection or meditation. It teaches that by developing a deep understanding of life's dualities and maintaining spiritual equilibrium, one can navigate through life's challenges with clarity and purpose, avoiding confusion and making wise decisions in all situations.

shlokas.name: Shloka 28
shlokas.interpretation: This verse emphasizes the superiority of yoga and spiritual knowledge over ritualistic practices. It suggests that while Vedic rituals, sacrifices, austerities, and charitable acts yield merit, a yogi who understands the supreme truth transcends all these. The verse highlights the importance of direct spiritual realization over mere religious observances, indicating that true spiritual knowledge leads to the highest state of consciousness.
shlokas.life_application: This verse encourages individuals to look beyond external religious practices and focus on inner spiritual growth. It can be applied in daily life by prioritizing self-reflection, meditation, and the pursuit of higher knowledge over mere ritualistic observances. It teaches that true spiritual progress comes from understanding the essence of existence rather than following religious customs blindly. This approach can lead to a more meaningful and purposeful life, helping individuals to overcome stress, find inner peace, and achieve a higher state of consciousness in their everyday experiences.

chapters.name: Raja Vidya Yoga
chapters.summary: Chapter 9 of the Bhagavad Gita, known as Raja Vidya Yoga or the Yoga of Royal Knowledge and Royal Secret, focuses on the supreme knowledge of God. Krishna reveals his divine nature and emphasizes the importance of devotion and surrender to him. He explains how he pervades all creation, sustains it, and yet remains detached from it.
chapters.main_theme: The supremacy of devotion (Bhakti) to Krishna as the path to spiritual realization and liberation
philosophical_aspects: The omnipresence and transcendence of God
The relationship between the Divine and creation
The concept of Maya (divine illusion)
The equality of all beings in the eyes of God
The power of devotion and faith
The nature of karma and its consequences
The importance of surrender to the Divine
life_problems_addressed: How to attain spiritual knowledge and liberation
Overcoming doubts about the nature of God
Finding purpose and meaning in life
Dealing with the cycle of birth and death
Understanding the relationship between individual actions and cosmic order
Resolving conflicts between worldly duties and spiritual aspirations
Cultivating a personal relationship with the Divine

chapters.philosophical_progression: The chapter begins with Krishna introducing the most confidential knowledge. It then progresses to explain the omnipresence and transcendence of the Divine, followed by the cyclical nature of creation and karma. The discourse then shifts to the superiority of devotional service (Bhakti Yoga) over ritualistic worship, emphasizing the importance of surrender and devotion to the Divine. The chapter concludes by highlighting the universal accessibility of spiritual realization and the transformative power of devotion.
chapters.chapter_relevance: Chapter 9 is crucial in the Bhagavad Gita as it reveals the most confidential knowledge about the nature of God and the path of devotion. It establishes Krishna as the Supreme Being and emphasizes Bhakti Yoga as the highest form of spiritual practice. This chapter bridges the philosophical concepts introduced earlier with the more devotional teachings that follow, making it a pivotal point in the overall narrative of the Gita.

shlokas.name: Shloka 1
shlokas.interpretation: This verse marks the beginning of Chapter 9, where Krishna introduces the most confidential knowledge to Arjuna. It emphasizes the importance of receiving wisdom with a non-envious attitude. Krishna promises to reveal both theoretical knowledge (jnana) and realized knowledge (vijnana), indicating a comprehensive understanding that goes beyond mere intellectual grasp. The verse also highlights the transformative power of this knowledge, capable of liberating one from all inauspiciousness.
shlokas.life_application: This verse teaches us the importance of approaching knowledge with humility and without envy. In daily life, we can apply this by being open-minded and receptive to new ideas and perspectives, especially from those more experienced or knowledgeable than us. It also emphasizes the value of both theoretical and practical knowledge in solving life's problems. By cultivating a non-envious attitude and seeking comprehensive understanding, we can gain insights that help us overcome personal struggles and achieve spiritual growth.

shlokas.name: Shloka 2
shlokas.interpretation: This verse emphasizes the supreme nature of spiritual knowledge, describing it as the king of all sciences and the most confidential of all secrets. It suggests that this knowledge is directly perceivable, in alignment with dharma (righteousness), and leads to eternal happiness. The verse implies that this spiritual wisdom is not just theoretical but can be practically experienced and applied in one's life, leading to lasting fulfillment.
shlokas.life_application: This verse encourages individuals to pursue spiritual knowledge as the highest form of education. It can be applied in daily life by prioritizing self-reflection and spiritual practices over mundane pursuits. By focusing on this supreme knowledge, one can find lasting happiness and purpose, overcome life's challenges with a broader perspective, and align one's actions with dharma or righteous living. This approach can lead to better decision-making, reduced stress, and a more fulfilling life overall.

अव्ययम्
इति। न अस्य फलतः कर्मवत् व्ययः अस्तीति अव्ययम्। अतः श्रद्धेयम् आत्मज्ञानम्।।ये पुनः --,
commentaries.madhvacharya: ।।राजविद्या प्रधानविद्या। प्रत्यक्षं ब्रह्म अवगम्यते येन तत्प्रत्यक्षावगमम्। अक्षेष्विन्द्रियेषु प्रति प्रतिस्थित इति प्रत्यक्षः। तथा च श्रुतिः यः प्राणे तिष्ठन्प्राणादन्तरो यं प्राणो न वेद यस्य प्राणः शरीरम्। यः प्राणमन्तरो यमयत्येष त आत्माऽन्तर्याम्यमृतः। यो वाचि तिष्ठन् ৷৷. यश्चक्षुषि तिष्ठन् [बृ.उ.3।7।1618] इत्यादिः। य एषोऽन्तरक्षिणि पुरुषो दृश्यते [छां.उ.1।7।5] इति च अङ्गुष्ठमात्रः पुरुषोऽङ्गुष्ठं च समाश्रितः [म.ना.उ.15।5] इति च।त्वं मनस्त्वं चन्द्रमास्त्वं चक्षुरादित्यः इत्यादेश्च मोक्षधर्मे। [म.भा.12।338।98100] स प्रत्यक्षः प्रति इति हि सोऽक्षेष्वक्षवान् भवति य एवं विद्वान्प्रत्यक्षं वेद इति सामवेदे बाभ्रव्यशाखायाम्। धर्मो भगवान् तद्विषयं धर्म्यम्। सर्वं जगद्धत्त इति धर्मः।पृथिवी धर्ममूर्धनि इति च प्रयोगान्मोक्षधर्मे।भारभृत्कथितो योगी [म.भा.13।149।106] इति च। भर्ता सन् भ्रियमाणो बिभर्ति [तै.आ.3।14] इति च श्रुतिः। धर्मो वा इदमग्र आसीन्न पृथिवी न वायुर्भाकाशो न ब्रह्मा न रुद्रो न देवा न ऋषयः सोऽध्यायत् इति च सामवेदशाखायाम्।
commentaries.ramanujacharya:
।।
राजविद्या
विद्यानां राजा
राजगुह्यं
गुह्यानां राजा राज्ञां विद्येति वा राजविद्या? राजानो हि विस्तीर्णागाधमनसः? महामनसाम् इयं विद्या इत्यर्थः।महामनस एव गोपनीयगोपनकुशला इति तेषाम् एव गुह्यम्
इदम्। उत्तमम् पवित्रं
मत्प्राप्तिविरोध्यशेषकल्मषापहं
प्रत्यक्षावगमम्?
अवगम्यते इति अवगमो विषयः? प्रत्यक्षभूतः अवगमो विषयो यस्य ज्ञानस्य तत् प्रत्यक्षावगमम्? भक्तिरूपेण उपासनेन उपास्यमानः अहं तदानीम् एव उपासितुः प्रत्यक्षताम् उपागतो भवामि इत्यर्थः।अथापि
धर्म्यं
धर्माद् अनपेतं धर्मत्वं हि निःश्रेयससाधनत्वम् स्वरूपेण एव अत्यर्थप्रियत्वेन तदानीम् एव मद्दर्शनापादनतया च स्वयं निःश्रेयसरूपम् अपि निरतिशयनिःश्रेयसरूपात्यन्तिकमत्प्राप्तिसाधनम् इत्यर्थः। अत एव
सुसुखं
कर्तुं सुसुखोपादानम्? अत्यर्थप्रियत्वेन उपादेयम्
अव्ययम्
अक्षयं मत्प्राप्तिं साधयित्वा अपि स्वयं न क्षीयते। एवंरूपम् उपासनं कुर्वतो मत्प्रदाने कृते अपि न किञ्चित् कृतं मया अस्य इति मे प्रतिभाति इत्यर्थः।

प्रत्यक्षावगमं धर्म्यं सुसुखं कर्तुमव्ययम्
shlokas.transliteration:

shlokas.meaning: This is the Premier Science, the Sovereign Secret, the Purest and Best; intuitional, righteous; and to him who practiseth it pleasant beyond measure.

shlokas.name: Shloka 3
shlokas.interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of faith (shraddha) in spiritual practice. It warns that those who lack faith in the teachings of Krishna (dharma) fail to attain the ultimate goal of self-realization. The cycle of birth and death (samsara) is described as a path of death, highlighting the urgency of spiritual awakening. The verse implies that faith is crucial for transcending material existence and reaching the divine.
shlokas.life_application: This verse can be applied to cultivate perseverance and commitment in one's spiritual journey or personal growth. It encourages individuals to develop faith in their chosen path, whether spiritual or secular, to achieve their goals. In practical terms, it suggests that doubt and skepticism can hinder progress and keep one trapped in unproductive cycles. By fostering faith and dedication, one can overcome obstacles and achieve transformative results in various aspects of life, such as career, relationships, or personal development.

shlokas.meaning: They who have no faith in this teaching cannot find Me, but remain lost in the purlieus of this perishable world.

shlokas.name: Shloka 4
shlokas.interpretation: This verse encapsulates the concept of God's omnipresence and transcendence. Krishna explains His relationship with the universe, emphasizing that He pervades all of creation while remaining distinct from it. This paradoxical nature of the Divine is a fundamental concept in Vedantic philosophy, illustrating the simultaneous immanence and transcendence of the Supreme Being.
shlokas.life_application: Understanding this verse can help individuals develop a broader perspective on life and their place in the universe. It encourages seeing the divine in all things while recognizing that the ultimate reality transcends physical manifestations. This can lead to greater respect for all forms of life, reduced ego, and a sense of interconnectedness, which can be applied in daily interactions, environmental consciousness, and personal spiritual practices.

translation.purohitSwami: The whole world is pervaded by Me, yet My form is not seen. All living things have their being in Me, yet I am not limited by them.

commentaries.shankaracharya:
।। --,
मया
मम यः परो भावः तेन
ततं
व्याप्तं

मत्स्थानि? सर्वभूतानि
ब्रह्मादीनि स्तम्बपर्यन्तानि। न हि निरात्मकं किञ्चित् भूतं व्यवहाराय अवकल्पते। अतः मत्स्थानि मया आत्मना आत्मवत्त्वेन स्थितानि? अतः मयि स्थितानि इति उच्यन्ते। तेषां भूतानाम् अहमेव आत्मा इत्यतः तेषु स्थितः इति मूढबुद्धीनां अवभासते अतः ब्रवीमि --
न च अहं
तेषु भूतेषु
अवस्थितः?
मूर्तवत् संश्लेषाभावेन आकाशस्यापि अन्तरतमो हि अहम्। न हि असंसर्गि वस्तु क्वचित् आधेयभावेन अवस्थितं भवति।।अत एव असंसर्गित्वात् मम --,

shlokas.name: Shloka 5
shlokas.interpretation: This verse reveals the paradoxical nature of Krishna's relationship with the universe. It emphasizes the concept of divine omnipresence while maintaining a distinct identity. Krishna explains His supreme yogic power, which allows Him to sustain all beings without being limited by them. This verse highlights the transcendental nature of the Supreme Being, who is simultaneously immanent and transcendent.
shlokas.life_application: This verse can help individuals understand the complex nature of reality and their relationship with the divine. It encourages a broader perspective on life, reminding us that we are supported by a higher power while maintaining our individuality. This understanding can lead to a sense of security and purpose, reducing anxiety about existence. It also inspires us to recognize the divine in all things while understanding that the divine transcends all manifestations, promoting respect for all life forms and the environment.

shlokas.meaning: Nevertheless, they do not consciously abide in Me. Such is My Divine Sovereignty that though I, the Supreme Self, am the cause and upholder of all, yet I remain outside.

shlokas.name: Shloka 6
shlokas.interpretation: This verse presents a profound analogy between the omnipresence of air within space and the existence of all beings within the Supreme. It illustrates the concept of divine immanence, suggesting that just as air pervades all of space without being bound by it, the Supreme Being permeates and sustains all of creation without being limited by it. This metaphor helps to explain the simultaneous transcendence and immanence of the Divine, a fundamental concept in Vedantic philosophy.
shlokas.life_application: This verse can help individuals develop a sense of interconnectedness with all of existence, fostering compassion and respect for all life forms. It encourages a broader perspective on personal challenges, reminding us that we are part of a larger cosmic order. This understanding can reduce ego-centric thinking and promote a more harmonious approach to relationships and environmental stewardship. It also offers comfort in difficult times by emphasizing our constant connection to the divine, potentially alleviating feelings of isolation or meaninglessness.

shlokas.name: Shloka 7
shlokas.interpretation: This verse reveals the cyclical nature of creation and dissolution in the universe. It emphasizes Lord Krishna's role as the supreme controller who oversees these cosmic cycles. The shloka highlights the concept of prakriti (material nature) and its relationship with the Divine, suggesting that all beings are ultimately part of the Lord's nature and return to it at the end of each cosmic cycle, only to be manifested again at the beginning of the next.
shlokas.life_application: This verse can help individuals understand the impermanence of material existence and the eternal nature of the soul. It encourages detachment from worldly possessions and outcomes, as everything is part of a larger cosmic cycle. This perspective can aid in reducing stress and anxiety about temporary situations, promoting a more balanced and spiritual approach to life's challenges. It also instills a sense of humility and reverence for the divine order, encouraging individuals to align their actions with universal principles.

shlokas.name: Shloka 8
shlokas.interpretation: This verse reveals the cyclical nature of creation and the divine role of Krishna in this process. It emphasizes the concept of prakriti (material nature) and how all beings are subject to its influence. Krishna, as the Supreme Being, oversees this process but remains detached from it, highlighting the interplay between the divine and the material world.
shlokas.life_application: This verse can help individuals understand the impermanence of material existence and the power of natural laws. It encourages acceptance of life's cycles and challenges while promoting detachment from outcomes. In practical terms, it can guide people to focus on their actions (karma) rather than results, fostering resilience and equanimity in the face of life's ups and downs. It also prompts reflection on the balance between free will and the influence of external factors in shaping one's life journey.

bhūtagrāmamimaṅ kṛtsnamavaśaṅ prakṛtērvaśāt
shlokas.meaning: With the help of Nature, again and again I pour forth the whole multitude of beings, whether they will or no, for they are ruled by My Will.

shlokas.name: Shloka 9
shlokas.interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of non-attachment and the transcendental nature of the Divine. It illustrates that the Supreme Being, while being the source of all actions, remains unaffected by them. This paradox of being involved yet detached is a key aspect of Krishna's divinity and serves as a model for human behavior in the material world.
shlokas.life_application: This verse teaches us to perform our duties without being overly attached to the results. By adopting a mindset of detachment, we can reduce stress, anxiety, and disappointment in our daily lives. It encourages us to act with dedication and skill, but to remain emotionally unaffected by success or failure, thus maintaining inner peace and equanimity in all situations.

shlokas.name: Shloka 10
shlokas.interpretation: This verse reveals the cosmic order and the supreme control of the Divine. It emphasizes that while nature (Prakriti) operates, it does so under the supervision of the Supreme Being. This highlights the concept of divine governance in the universe, where even the most fundamental processes of creation and dissolution are overseen by a higher power. The verse also touches upon the cyclical nature of the universe, implying that the world goes through continuous cycles of creation and destruction under this divine supervision.
shlokas.life_application: This verse can help individuals understand their place in the grand scheme of things, fostering humility and a sense of purpose. It encourages one to recognize the divine order in all aspects of life, promoting acceptance of both favorable and unfavorable circumstances. In practical terms, it can inspire people to perform their duties diligently while acknowledging a higher power, leading to reduced stress and anxiety about outcomes. It also promotes environmental consciousness by emphasizing the divine nature of the world around us.

shlokas.name: Shloka 11
shlokas.interpretation: This verse highlights the divine nature of Krishna and the ignorance of those who fail to recognize it. It emphasizes the concept of God incarnating in human form and the spiritual blindness that prevents people from perceiving the supreme reality behind the apparent physical manifestation. The shloka underscores the importance of spiritual wisdom and the ability to see beyond material appearances.
shlokas.life_application: This verse teaches us to look beyond superficial appearances and seek deeper spiritual truths. In daily life, it encourages us to approach people and situations with an open mind, recognizing that there may be more than what meets the eye. It also reminds us to cultivate spiritual wisdom and discernment to recognize the divine in various forms around us, promoting respect and understanding in our interactions with others.

commentaries.madhvacharya: ।।तर्हि केचित्कथं त्वामवजानन्ति का च तेषां गतिः इत्यत आह -- अवजानन्तीत्यादिना। मानुषीं तनुं? मूढानां मानुषवत्प्रतीतां तनुं? न तु मनुष्यरूपाम्। उक्तं च मोक्षधर्मेयत्किञ्चिदिह लोकेऽस्मिन्देहबद्धं विशाम्पते। सर्वं पञ्चभिराविष्टं भूतैरीश्वरबुद्धिजैः। ईश्वरो हि जगत्स्रष्टा प्रभुर्नारायणो विराट्। भूतान्तरात्मा वग्दः सगुणो निर्गुणोऽपि च। भूतप्रलयमव्यक्तं शुश्रूषु(शुणुष्व) -- र्नृपसत्तम [म.भा.12।347।1113] इति। अवतारप्रसङ्गे चैतदुक्तम्। अतो नावताराः पृथक् शङ्क्याः।रूपाण्यनेकान्यसृजत्प्रादुर्भावभवाय सः। वाराहं नारसिंहं च वामनं मानुषं तथा [म.भा.12।349।37] इति। तत्रैव प्रथमसर्गकाल एवावताररूपविभक्त्युक्तेः। अतो न तेषां मानुषत्वादिर्विना भ्रान्तिम्। भूतं महदीश्वरं चेति भूतमहेश्वरम्। तथा हि (सामवेदे) बाभ्रव्यशाखायाम् -- अनाद्यनन्तं परिपूर्णरूपमीशं वराणामपि देववीर्यम् इति। अस्य महतो भूतस्य निश्श्वसितम् [बृ.उ.2।4।10] इति च।ब्रह्मपुरोहित ब्रह्मकायिक राजिक महाराजिकं --  इति च मोक्षधर्मे [म.भा.12।338नाम4043]।

shlokas.name: Shloka 12
shlokas.interpretation: This verse describes the nature of those who are deluded and have turned away from the divine. It emphasizes the futility of their aspirations, actions, and knowledge when they are not aligned with spiritual truth. The shloka suggests that such individuals, by embracing demonic qualities, are trapped in a cycle of delusion and ignorance, unable to perceive the higher reality of existence.
shlokas.life_application: This verse serves as a warning against pursuing materialistic goals without spiritual awareness. It encourages self-reflection to identify and overcome deluding tendencies in one's life. By recognizing the futility of actions driven by ego and ignorance, individuals can redirect their efforts towards meaningful spiritual growth, cultivate true knowledge, and develop discernment in their choices and actions.

commentaries.madhvacharya: ।।तेषां फलमाह -- मोघाशा इति। वृथाशाः? भगवद्वेषिभिराशासितं न किञ्चिदाप्यते। यज्ञादिकर्माणि च वृथैव तेषां? ज्ञानं च। केनापि ब्रह्मरुद्रादिभक्त्याद्युपायेन न कश्चित् पुरुषार्थ आमुष्मिकस्तैराप्यत इत्यर्थः। वक्ष्यति चतानहं द्विषतः क्रूरान् संसारेषु नराधमान् [16।16] इत्यादि। मोक्षधर्मे च [म.भा.12।346।6?7]कर्मणा मनसा वाचा यो द्विष्याद्विष्णुमव्ययम्। मज्जन्ति पितरस्तस्य नरके शाश्वतीः समाः। यो द्विष्याद्विबुधश्रेष्ठं देवं नारायणं हरिम्। कथं स न भवेद्वेष्य आलोकान्तस्य (आत्मा लोकस्य) कस्यचित् इति। सर्वोत्कृष्टे ज्ञानभक्ती हि यस्य नारायणे पुष्करविष्टराद्ये। सर्वावमे द्वेषयुतश्च तस्मिन्भ्रूणानन्तघ्नोऽस्य समो न चैव इति सामवेदे शाण्डिल्यशाखायाम्।द्वेषाच्चैद्यादयो नृपाः [भाग.7।1।30]वैरणं यं नृपतयः शिशुपालपौण्ड्रशाल्वादयो गतिविलासविलोकनाद्यैः। ध्यायन्त आकृतधियः शयनासनादौ तत्साम्यमीयुरनुरक्तधियः पुनः किम् [11।5।48] इति भागवते। भक्तिप्रियत्वज्ञापनार्थं नित्यध्यानस्तुत्यर्थं च? स्वभक्तस्य कदाचिच्छापबलात् द्वेषिणोऽपि भक्तिफलमेव भगवान्ददातीति।भक्ता एव हि ते पूर्वं शिशुपालादयः शापबलात् द्वेषिणः। तत्प्रश्नपूर्वं पार्षदत्वशापादिकथनाच्चैतज्ज्ञायते। अन्यथा किमिति तदप्रस्तुतमुच्यते। भगवतः साम्यकथनं तु द्वेषिणामपि द्वेषमनिरूप्य पूर्वतनभक्तिफलमेव ददातीति ज्ञापयितुम्।न मे भक्तः प्रणश्यति [9।31] इति वक्ष्यति। न चभावो हि भवकारणं इत्यादिविरोधः। द्वेषभाविनां द्वेष एव भवतीति हि युक्तम्। अन्यथा गुरुद्वेषिणामपि गुरुत्वं भवतीत्यनिष्टमापद्येत। न चाकृतधीत्वे विशेषः? तेषामेव हिरण्यकशिप्वादीनां पापप्रतीतेः।हिरण्यकशिपुश्चापि भगवन्निन्दया तमः। विविक्षुरत्यगात्सूनोः प्रह्लादस्यानुभावतः [भाग.4।21।47] इति।यदनिन्दत्पिता मह्यं (मे त्वां) इत्यारभ्यतस्मात्पिता मे पूयेत दुरन्ताद्दुस्तरादघात् [भाग.7।10।1517] इति प्रह्लादेन भगवतो वरयाचनाच्च। बहुषु ग्रन्थेषु च निषेधः। कुत्रचिदेव तदुक्तिरिति विशेषः। यस्मिंस्तदुच्यते तत्रैव निषेध उक्तः।महातात्पर्यविरोधश्चोक्तः पुरस्तात्। अयुक्तिमद्भ्यो युक्तिमन्त्येव बलवन्ति वाक्यानि। युक्तयश्चोक्ता अन्येषाम्। न चैषां काचिद्गतिः। साम्येऽपि वाक्ययोर्लोकानुकूलाननुकूलयोर्लोकानुकूलमेव बलवत्। लोकानुकूलं भक्तप्रियत्वं च नेतरत्। उक्तं च तेषां भक्तत्वम्।मन्ये सुरान्भागवतांस्त्र्यधीशे संरम्भमार्गाभिनिविष्टचित्तान् [भाग.3।1।24] इत्यादि। अतो न भगवद्वेषिणां काचिद्गतिरिति सिद्धम्। द्वेषकारणमाह -- राक्षसीमिति।

shlokas.meaning: Their hopes are vain, their actions worthless, their knowledge futile; they are without sense, deceitful, barbarous and godless.

shlokas.name: Shloka 13
shlokas.interpretation: This verse highlights the characteristics of great souls (mahātmās) who have realized the divine nature of the Supreme. It emphasizes their unwavering devotion and complete surrender to the Divine, recognizing the Lord as the eternal source of all existence. The verse also implies the contrast between these enlightened beings and those still bound by material nature.
shlokas.life_application: This verse teaches us the importance of cultivating a higher consciousness and aligning ourselves with divine qualities. It encourages us to develop unwavering focus in our spiritual practices, reminding us that true fulfillment comes from connecting with the eternal source. In daily life, we can apply this by striving to maintain a broader perspective, remaining steadfast in our principles, and dedicating our actions to a higher purpose, which can lead to greater inner peace and resilience in facing life's challenges.

shlokas.name: Shloka 14
shlokas.interpretation: This verse describes the characteristics of true devotees who are constantly engaged in devotional service to Krishna. It emphasizes the importance of continuous practice, firm determination, and unwavering devotion in spiritual life. The verse highlights four key aspects of devotion: glorification, endeavor, reverence, and worship, all performed with steadfast dedication and love.
shlokas.life_application: This verse teaches us the importance of consistency and dedication in our spiritual practices and personal growth. It encourages us to cultivate a habit of gratitude, perseverance in our goals, humility in our approach, and devotion in our actions. By applying these principles in daily life, one can develop resilience, maintain focus on important objectives, build stronger relationships, and find greater purpose and fulfillment.

shlokas.name: Shloka 15
shlokas.interpretation: This verse highlights the diverse ways in which devotees approach and worship the Divine. It emphasizes that some seekers worship through the sacrifice of knowledge (jnana yajna), recognizing the Supreme in various forms - as one (non-dual), as separate (dualistic), or as manifested in multiple forms throughout the universe. This verse underscores the inclusivity and flexibility of spiritual paths in Hinduism, acknowledging that different individuals may have different approaches to understanding and connecting with the Divine, all of which are valid.
shlokas.life_application: This verse encourages respect for diverse spiritual practices and beliefs. It teaches us to be open-minded and accepting of different philosophical viewpoints, fostering harmony in a pluralistic society. In personal spiritual growth, it inspires us to explore various approaches to understanding the Divine, allowing for a more comprehensive and nuanced spiritual journey. In conflict resolution, this verse reminds us that seemingly contradictory views can be different perspectives of the same truth, promoting tolerance and understanding.

shlokas.meaning: Others worship Me with full consciousness as the One, the Manifold, the Omnipresent, the Universal.

shlokas.name: Shloka 16
shlokas.interpretation: This verse emphasizes the all-pervasive nature of the Divine. Krishna declares Himself as the essence of all aspects of Vedic rituals and sacrifices, highlighting the omnipresence of the Supreme Being in every element of spiritual practice. It underscores the unity of all forms of worship and the ultimate reality behind diverse religious expressions.
shlokas.life_application: This verse teaches us to see the divine in all aspects of life, not just in formal religious practices. It encourages a holistic spiritual outlook, where every action can be seen as an offering to the Divine. This perspective can help in cultivating mindfulness, respect for all things, and a sense of unity with the universe, leading to a more harmonious and purposeful life.

shlokas.name: Shloka 17
shlokas.interpretation: This verse emphasizes the all-encompassing nature of the Divine. Krishna declares Himself as the ultimate source and sustainer of the entire creation, embodying both masculine and feminine aspects. He is not only the immediate parent but also the grand-parent, highlighting His eternal nature. The verse also connects the Divine to sacred knowledge and purification, showing that spiritual wisdom and purity are inherent in the Supreme Being.
shlokas.life_application: This verse can help individuals develop a holistic perspective on life, recognizing the divine presence in all aspects of existence. It encourages respect for knowledge and purity, which can guide ethical decision-making. Understanding the interconnectedness of all things can foster a sense of responsibility towards the world and its inhabitants. The concept of divine parenthood can provide comfort during difficult times, reminding one of the ever-present support of the Supreme.

shlokas.name: Shloka 18
shlokas.interpretation: This verse emphasizes the all-encompassing nature of the Divine. It portrays the Supreme Being as the ultimate source and destination of all existence, highlighting the intimate relationship between the Divine and creation. The verse underscores the omnipresence and omnipotence of the Divine, suggesting that every aspect of existence is permeated by and dependent on the Supreme.
shlokas.life_application: This verse can help individuals develop a sense of security and trust in the Divine, knowing that the Supreme is present in all aspects of life. It encourages seeking guidance and support from the Divine in times of difficulty, viewing challenges as part of a larger cosmic process. The teaching can also inspire people to cultivate a friendship with the Divine, fostering a sense of companionship and reducing feelings of loneliness or isolation. Moreover, it can motivate individuals to recognize the divine presence in all beings, promoting compassion and unity in their interactions with others.

translation.purohitSwami: I am the Goal, the Sustainer, the Lord, the Witness, the Home, the Shelter, the Lover and the Origin; I am Life and Death; I am the Fountain and the Seed Imperishable.

commentaries.madhvacharya: ।।गम्यते मुमुक्षुभिरिति गतिः। तथा हि सामवेदे वासिष्ठशाखायाम् अथ कस्मादुच्यते गतिरिति ब्रह्मैव गतिरिति तद्धि गम्यते पापविमुक्तैः इति। साक्षादीक्षत इति साक्षी। तथाहि बाष्कलशाखायाम् स साक्षादिदमद्राक्षीद्यदद्राक्षीत्तत्साक्षिणः साक्षित्वम् इति। शरणमाश्रयः संसारभीतस्य।परं परायणं इत्याद्युक्तम्। नारायणं महाज्ञेयं विश्वात्मानं परायणम् [म.ना.उ.9।3] इति च। संहारकाले प्रकृत्या जगदत्र निधीयत इति निधानम्। तथा हि ऋग्वेदखिलेषु अपश्यमप्यये मायया विश्वकर्मण्यदो जगन्निहितं शुभ्रचक्षुः इति।

shlokas.name: Shloka 19
shlokas.interpretation: This verse emphasizes the all-encompassing nature of the Divine. Krishna reveals himself as the source of all natural phenomena and the ultimate controller of life and death. It illustrates the concept of God's immanence in every aspect of existence, from the most mundane to the most profound. The verse also touches on the philosophical idea of duality and non-duality, suggesting that the Divine transcends these apparent opposites.
shlokas.life_application: This verse can help individuals develop a broader perspective on life's experiences. By recognizing the divine presence in all aspects of existence, one can cultivate acceptance and equanimity in the face of both positive and negative circumstances. It encourages us to see beyond surface-level dualities and find unity in diversity, which can lead to greater tolerance and understanding in personal relationships and society at large. Moreover, it reminds us of the impermanence of worldly phenomena, inspiring detachment and a focus on spiritual growth.

shlokas.name: Shloka 20
shlokas.interpretation: This verse highlights the limitations of ritualistic worship and the pursuit of temporary heavenly pleasures. It suggests that those who perform Vedic rituals with the aim of gaining celestial rewards are still bound by the cycle of karma and rebirth. Krishna implies that such actions, while not inherently wrong, fall short of the ultimate goal of spiritual realization and union with the Divine.
shlokas.life_application: This verse teaches us to examine our motivations in spiritual practices. It encourages us to look beyond short-term gains and material rewards in our spiritual journey. Instead of focusing on temporary pleasures or status, we should aim for lasting spiritual growth and self-realization. In daily life, this principle can be applied by prioritizing long-term personal development over quick fixes or temporary solutions, and by cultivating a deeper understanding of our actions and their consequences.

shlokas.name: Shloka 21
shlokas.interpretation: This verse highlights the cyclical nature of karma and the temporary nature of heavenly pleasures. It emphasizes that actions performed with desire for rewards lead to a continuous cycle of birth and death. The verse indirectly encourages seekers to aim for liberation (moksha) rather than temporary celestial enjoyments.
shlokas.life_application: This verse teaches us to focus on long-term spiritual growth rather than short-term pleasures. In daily life, it encourages us to make choices based on lasting values and inner growth, rather than temporary gains or sensory satisfactions. It also reminds us that actions driven by desire for rewards will keep us bound in cycles of temporary happiness and inevitable disappointment, urging us to cultivate detachment and seek higher spiritual goals.

shlokas.name: Shloka 22
shlokas.interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of unwavering devotion and complete surrender to the Divine. It suggests that those who focus their thoughts entirely on God, without any distractions or divided loyalties, receive special care and protection. The Lord personally takes responsibility for the well-being of such devotees, both in terms of their spiritual progress (yoga) and material needs (kshema). This verse is often seen as a powerful assurance of divine grace and protection for sincere devotees.
shlokas.life_application: This verse can be applied in daily life to cultivate trust in a higher power and reduce anxiety about worldly concerns. It encourages individuals to focus on their spiritual growth and duties while having faith that their essential needs will be met. This teaching can help in managing stress, overcoming fear of scarcity, and developing a more balanced approach to material pursuits. It also promotes the idea of living in the present moment with complete dedication to one's chosen path or duty, trusting that sincere efforts will be supported by the universe or divine forces.

shlokas.meaning: But if a man will meditate on Me and Me alone, and will worship Me always and everywhere, I will take upon Myself the fulfillment of his aspiration, and I will safeguard whatsoever he shall attain.

shlokas.name: Shloka 23
shlokas.interpretation: This verse highlights the inclusive nature of Krishna's teachings, emphasizing that all forms of worship, even those directed towards other deities, ultimately reach Him. It underscores the unity of divine consciousness and the idea that there are many paths to the same ultimate truth. Krishna acknowledges the sincerity of devotees who worship other gods, suggesting that their devotion, though not directly aimed at Him, still reaches Him indirectly.
shlokas.life_application: This verse teaches us to respect and tolerate different religious beliefs and practices. It encourages us to look beyond superficial differences in worship and recognize the underlying unity in all spiritual pursuits. In daily life, this can be applied by fostering interfaith dialogue, practicing religious tolerance, and understanding that different cultural and spiritual practices can lead to the same ultimate goal of self-realization and connection with the divine.

shlokas.name: Shloka 24
shlokas.interpretation: This verse emphasizes the supreme position of Krishna as the ultimate recipient and lord of all sacrifices. It highlights the importance of recognizing the divine nature of Krishna in spiritual practices. The verse also points out the consequence of failing to understand this truth, which leads to the cycle of rebirth and suffering.
shlokas.life_application: This teaching encourages individuals to perform their duties and rituals with the right understanding and attitude. It emphasizes the importance of dedicating one's actions to the Divine, which can lead to a more purposeful and spiritually fulfilling life. By recognizing the supreme nature of the Divine in all aspects of life, one can overcome ego, reduce attachment to results, and find greater peace and contentment in daily activities.

shlokas.name: Shloka 25
shlokas.interpretation: This verse emphasizes the principle of spiritual reciprocity and the law of karma. It illustrates that one's devotional focus and worship determine their spiritual destination. The shloka underscores the importance of one's chosen path of devotion and how it aligns with their ultimate spiritual goal. It also subtly hints at the superiority of devotion to Krishna (the speaker) as the path to the highest spiritual attainment.
shlokas.life_application: This verse can guide individuals in choosing their spiritual path wisely, understanding that their focus and devotion shape their spiritual journey and ultimate destination. It encourages self-reflection on one's spiritual practices and goals. In practical terms, it teaches that our thoughts, actions, and devotions should align with our highest aspirations, whether in spiritual pursuits or worldly endeavors. This principle can be applied in career choices, relationship building, and personal development, reminding us that our consistent efforts and focus in any area of life will yield corresponding results.

shlokas.name: Shloka 26
shlokas.interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of devotion and sincerity in offering to the Divine. It suggests that the act of offering is more significant than the material value of the offering itself. The verse illustrates the accessibility of the Divine to all, regardless of their material possessions or social status. It also highlights the reciprocal nature of the devotee-Divine relationship, where genuine devotion is met with divine acceptance and grace.
shlokas.life_application: This teaching can be applied in daily life by emphasizing the importance of intention and sincerity in our actions, rather than their grandeur or material value. It encourages us to approach our work, relationships, and spiritual practices with genuine love and devotion. This verse also teaches us to value and appreciate even the smallest acts of kindness or offerings from others, focusing on the sentiment behind the act rather than its material worth. It can help in cultivating gratitude, humility, and a non-judgmental attitude towards others' expressions of love or respect.

shlokas.name: Shloka 27
shlokas.interpretation: This verse encapsulates the essence of Karma Yoga, emphasizing the importance of dedicating all actions to the Divine. It suggests that every aspect of life, from the mundane to the spiritual, can be transformed into an act of worship when performed with the right attitude. This teaching encourages a holistic approach to spirituality, integrating it into daily life rather than separating it as a distinct activity.
shlokas.life_application: This verse can be applied to cultivate mindfulness and purpose in daily life. By viewing all actions as offerings to the Divine, one can find deeper meaning in work, relationships, and personal habits. It can help in overcoming stress and dissatisfaction by shifting focus from personal gain to a higher purpose. This approach can lead to greater contentment, reduced ego, and a more harmonious life by aligning one's actions with spiritual values.

shlokas.name: Shloka 28
shlokas.interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of detachment from the fruits of one's actions. It suggests that by performing actions with a spirit of renunciation and dedicating them to the Divine, one can break free from the cycle of karma. The verse also highlights the ultimate goal of spiritual practice: to attain union with the Supreme Being.
shlokas.life_application: This teaching can be applied in daily life by encouraging individuals to perform their duties without being overly attached to the outcomes. It promotes a mindset of working for the greater good rather than personal gain, which can reduce stress and anxiety related to results. By focusing on the action itself and dedicating it to a higher purpose, one can find more fulfillment in work and relationships, leading to a more balanced and peaceful life.

shlokas.name: Shloka 29
shlokas.interpretation: This verse emphasizes the impartial nature of the Divine and introduces the concept of reciprocal devotion. It highlights that while God treats all beings equally, those who approach with sincere devotion receive special attention. This doesn't contradict God's impartiality but illustrates the power of bhakti (devotion) in forging a deeper connection with the Divine.
shlokas.life_application: This verse teaches us to cultivate impartiality and equal respect for all beings in our daily interactions. It encourages developing a loving, devotional attitude towards life and work, which can lead to a deeper sense of connection and fulfillment. In challenging relationships, it reminds us to maintain equanimity while also inspiring us to forge deeper connections through sincere dedication and love.

shlokas.sanskrit_text:
समोऽहं सर्वभूतेषु न मे द्वेष्योऽस्ति न प्रियः।
ये भजन्ति तु मां भक्त्या मयि ते तेषु चाप्यहम्
shlokas.transliteration:
samō.haṅ sarvabhūtēṣu na mē dvēṣyō.sti na priyaḥ.
yē bhajanti tu māṅ bhaktyā mayi tē tēṣu cāpyaham
shlokas.meaning: I am the same to all beings. I favour none, and I hate none. But those who worship Me devotedly, they live in Me, and I in them.

shlokas.name: Shloka 30
shlokas.interpretation: This verse emphasizes the transformative power of devotion and the importance of one's current actions over past misdeeds. It suggests that even a person with a history of wrongdoing can be considered righteous if they wholeheartedly devote themselves to God. This teaches the concepts of redemption, the power of present choices, and the supremacy of devotion in spiritual life.
shlokas.life_application: This verse can be applied in situations where one needs to overcome past mistakes or judge others fairly. It encourages forgiveness, both of oneself and others, and emphasizes the importance of current choices over past actions. In personal development, it motivates individuals to make positive changes regardless of their history. In leadership and social contexts, it promotes giving second chances and valuing a person's present commitment over their past reputation.

shlokas.name: Shloka 31
shlokas.interpretation: This verse emphasizes the transformative power of devotion and the unwavering protection Krishna offers to his devotees. It highlights the swift spiritual progress one can make through sincere devotion, assuring that even those who have committed wrongs can quickly become righteous and find lasting peace. The verse serves as a powerful promise from Krishna, emphasizing the infallible nature of devotional service.
shlokas.life_application: This verse can be applied to overcome feelings of guilt, unworthiness, or hopelessness in one's spiritual journey. It encourages perseverance in devotional practices, assuring that sincere efforts lead to positive transformation. It can also be used to cultivate faith and trust in the divine, helping individuals face life's challenges with confidence and inner peace.

commentaries.madhvacharya: ।।कुतः क्षिप्रं भवति धर्मात्मा। देवदेवांशादिष्वेव च तद्भवति। उक्तं च सामवेदे शाण्डिल्यशाखायाम् -- नाविरतो दुश्चरितान्नाभक्तो नासमाहितः। सम्यग्भक्तो भवेत् कश्चिद्वासुदवेऽमलाशयः। देवर्षयस्तदंशाश्च भवन्ति क्वच ज्ञानतः इति। अतोऽन्यः कश्चिद्भवति चेत् दाम्भिकत्वेन सोऽनुमेयः। साधारणपापानां सत्सङ्गान्महत्यपि कथञ्चिद्भक्तिर्भवति। साधारणभक्तिर्वेतरेषाम्।स शठमतिरुपयाति योऽर्थतृष्णां तमधमचेष्टमवैहि नास्य भक्तिम् इति श्रीविष्णुपुराणे [3।7।30]सा श्रद्दधानस्य विवर्धमाना विरक्तिमन्यत्र करोति पुंसः इति च।वेदास्त्वधीता (वेदाः स्वधीताः) मम लोकनाथ तृप्तं तपो नानृतमुक्तपूर्वम्। पूजां गुरूणां सततं करोमि परस्य गुह्यं न च भिन्नपूर्वम्। गुप्तानि चत्वारि यथागमं (यथं) मे शत्रौ च मित्रे च समोऽस्मि नित्यम्। तं चापि (चादि -- ) देवं शरणं (सततं) प्रपन्नमेकान्तभावेन भजा(वृणो)म्यजस्रम्। एतैरुपायैः (एभिर्विशेषैः) परिशुद्धसत्त्वः कस्मान्न पश्येयमनन्तमेन(ईश)म् इति मोक्षधर्मे [म.भा.12।335।3?4?5]। आचारस्य ज्ञानसाधनत्वोक्तेश्च ज्ञानाभावे सम्यग्भक्त्यभावात्। तथा हि गौतमखिलेषु -- विना ज्ञानं कुतो भक्तिः कुतो भक्तिं विना च तत् इति।भक्तिः परेशानुभवो विरक्तिरन्यत्र चैतत्ित्रकमेककालम् इति च भागवते [11।2।42]।
