shlokas.name: Shloka 19
shlokas.interpretation: This verse describes Arjuna's vision of Krishna's cosmic form, emphasizing its infinite nature and all-encompassing presence. It highlights the transcendental aspect of the Divine, which is beyond the limitations of time and space. The imagery of countless arms, eyes like the sun and moon, and a face blazing like fire conveys the overwhelming power and omnipresence of the Supreme Being. This vision challenges Arjuna's previous understanding of Krishna and represents a pivotal moment in his spiritual awakening.
shlokas.life_application: This verse encourages us to broaden our perspective and recognize the divine presence in all aspects of existence. It teaches us to look beyond the apparent limitations of our physical world and connect with the infinite nature of consciousness. In practical terms, this can help in overcoming fear, developing a sense of unity with all beings, and cultivating humility by recognizing our place within the vast cosmic order. It also inspires awe and reverence, which can lead to a more mindful and respectful approach to life and nature.

translation.purohitSwami: Without beginning, without middle and without end, infinite in power, Thine arms all-embracing, the sun and moon Thine eyes, Thy face beaming with the fire of sacrifice, flooding the whole universe with light.

commentaries.shankaracharya:
।। --,
अनादिमध्यान्तम्
आदिश्च मध्यं च अन्तश्च न विद्यते यस्य सः अयम् अनादिमध्यान्तः तं त्वां अनादिमध्यान्तम्?
अनन्तवीर्यं
न तव वीर्यस्य अन्तः अस्ति इति अनन्तवीर्यः तं त्वाम् अनन्तवीर्यम्? तथा
अनन्तबाहुम्
अनन्ताः बाहवः यस्य तव सः त्वम्? अनन्तबाहुः तं त्वाम् अनन्तबाहुम्?
शशिसूर्यनेत्रं
शशिसूर्यौ नेत्रे यस्य तव सः त्वं शशिसूर्यनेत्रः तं त्वां शशिसूर्यनेत्रं चन्द्रादित्यनयनम्?
पश्यामि त्वां दीप्तहुताशवक्त्रं
दीप्तश्च असौ हुताशश्च वक्त्रं यस्य तव सः त्वं दीप्तहुताशवक्त्रः तं त्वां दीप्तहुताशवक्त्रम्?
स्वतेजसा विश्वम् इदं
समस्तं
तपन्तम्
।।
commentaries.madhvacharya: ।।शशिसूर्यनेत्रं इत्यपिअहं क्रतुः [9।16] इत्यादिवत्। तदङ्गजाः सर्वसुरादयोऽपि तस्मात्तदङ्गेत्यृषिभिः स्तुतास्ते इत्यृग्वेदखिलेषु। चन्द्रमा मनसो जातश्चक्षोः सूर्यो अजायत [ऋक्सं.8।4।19।3यजुस्सं.31।12] इति च। बहुरूपत्वाद्बह्वाश्रयत्वं तेषां युक्तम्।
commentaries.ramanujacharya:
।।
अनादिमध्यान्तम्
आदिमध्यान्तरहितम्?
अनन्तवीर्यम्
अनवधिकातिशयवीर्यम्? वीर्यशब्दः प्रदर्शनार्थः? अनवधिकातिशयज्ञानबलैश्वर्यशक्तितेजसां निधिम् इत्यर्थः।
अनन्तबाहुम्
असंख्येयबाहुम्? सोऽपि प्रदर्शनार्थः? अनन्तबाहूदरपादवक्त्रादिकम्?
शशिसूर्यनेत्रं
शशिवत् सूर्यवत् च प्रसादप्रतापयुक्तसर्वनेत्रम्? देवादीन् अनुकूलान् नमस्कारादि कुर्वाणान् प्रति प्रसादः? तद्विपरीतान् असुरराक्षसादीन् प्रति प्रतापःरक्षांसि भीतानि दिशो द्रवन्ति सर्वे नमस्यन्ति च सिद्धसंघाः।। (गीता 11।36) इति हि वक्ष्यते।
दीप्तहुताशवक्त्रं
प्रदीप्तकालानलवत् संहारानुगुणवक्त्रम्?
स्वतेजसा विश्वम् इदं तपन्तम्
-- तेजः पराभिभवनसामर्थ्यम्? स्वकीयेन तेजसा विश्वम् इदं तपन्तं
त्वां पश्यामि।
एवंभूतं सर्वस्य स्रष्टारम्? सर्वस्य आधारभूतं सर्वस्य प्रशासितारम्? सर्वस्य संहर्तारम्? ज्ञानाद्यपरिमितगुणसागरम्? आदिमध्यान्तरहितम् एवंभूतदिव्यदेहं त्वां यथोपदेशं साक्षात्करोमि इत्यर्थः।एकस्मिन् दिव्यदेहे अनेकोदरादिकं कथम्इत्थम् उपपद्यतेएकस्मात् कटिप्रदेशाद् अनन्तपरिमाणाद् ऊर्ध्वम् उद्गता यथोदितदिव्योदरादयः? अधश्च यथोदितदिव्यपादाः? तत्र एकस्मिन् मुखे नेत्रद्वयम् इति च न विरोधः।एवंभूतं त्वां दृष्ट्वा देवादयः अहं च प्रव्यथिता भवामि इति आह --

shlokas.sanskrit_text:
अनादिमध्यान्तमनन्तवीर्य
मनन्तबाहुं शशिसूर्यनेत्रम्।
पश्यामि त्वां दीप्तहुताशवक्त्रम्
स्वतेजसा विश्वमिदं तपन्तम्
shlokas.transliteration:
anādimadhyāntamanantavīrya-
manantabāhuṅ śaśisūryanētram.
paśyāmi tvāṅ dīptahutāśavaktram
svatējasā viśvamidaṅ tapantam
shlokas.meaning: Without beginning, without middle and without end, infinite in power, Thine arms all-embracing, the sun and moon Thine eyes, Thy face beaming with the fire of sacrifice, flooding the whole universe with light.

shlokas.name: Shloka 20
shlokas.interpretation: This verse describes Arjuna's awe and fear upon witnessing Krishna's cosmic form (Vishwaroop). It emphasizes the all-pervading nature of the Divine, spanning all directions and dimensions of existence. The shloka highlights the overwhelming power and magnificence of God's universal form, which instills both wonder and terror in the observer. It underscores the limitless nature of the Supreme Being and the insignificance of mortal existence in comparison.
shlokas.life_application: This verse can help individuals develop a sense of humility and cosmic perspective. It encourages us to recognize the vastness of the universe and our relatively small place within it, promoting a more balanced and less ego-centric approach to life. It can be applied to overcome personal fears and anxieties by realizing that our individual problems are minuscule in the grand scheme of things. Additionally, it can inspire a deeper respect for nature and the interconnectedness of all existence, promoting environmental consciousness and universal brotherhood.

scripts.kannada:
ದ್ಯಾವಾಪೃಥಿವ್ಯೋರಿದಮನ್ತರಂ ಹಿ
ವ್ಯಾಪ್ತಂ ತ್ವಯೈಕೇನ ದಿಶಶ್ಚ ಸರ್ವಾಃ.
ದೃಷ್ಟ್ವಾದ್ಭುತಂ ರೂಪಮುಗ್ರಂ ತವೇದಂ
ಲೋಕತ್ರಯಂ ಪ್ರವ್ಯಥಿತಂ ಮಹಾತ್ಮನ್

translation.purohitSwami: Alone thou fillest all the quarters of the sky, earth and heaven, and the regions between. O Almighty Lord! Seeing Thy marvellous and awe-inspiring Form, the spheres tremble with fear.

commentaries.shankaracharya:
।। --,
द्यावापृथिव्योः इदम् अन्तरं हि
अन्तरिक्षं
व्याप्तं त्वया एकेन
विश्वरूपधरेण
दिशश्च सर्वाः
व्याप्ताः।
दृष्ट्वा
उपलभ्य
अद्भुतं
विस्मापकं
रूपम् इदं तव उग्रं
क्रूरं लोकानां त्रयं
लोकत्रयं प्रव्यथितं
भीतं प्रचलितं वा हे
महात्मन्
अक्षुद्रस्वभाव।।
अथ अधुना पुरा यद्वा जयेम यदि वा नो जयेयुः (गीता 2।6) इति अर्जुनस्य यः संशयः आसीत्? तन्निर्णयाय पाण्डवजयम् ऐकान्तिकं दर्शयामि इति प्रवृत्तो भगवान्। तं पश्यन् आह --,किञ्च --,
commentaries.madhvacharya: ।।मातापित्रोरन्तरङ्गः स एकः? रूपेण चान्यैः सर्वगतः स एकः इति वारुणश्रुतेरेकेनैव द्यावापृथिव्योरन्तरं व्याप्तो भवति।पश्य मे पार्थ रूपाणि [1।6।18] इति बहूनि रूपाणि प्रतिज्ञातानि मातापितरौ च पृथिवीद्यावौ। मा नो माता पृथिवी दुर्मतौ धात् मधु द्यौरस्तु नः पिता [ऋक्सं.बृ.उ.6।3।6] इत्यादिप्रयोगात्। न तु नियमतो भयप्रदं तत्स्वरूपम्। नारदस्य तदभावात्। केषाञ्चित्तथा दर्शयति भगवान् -- प्रियन्ति केचित्तस्य रूपस्य दृष्टौ बिभेति कश्चिदभ्यसे सर्वतृप्तिः इति वारुणशाखायाम्। न तु तं सर्वे पश्यन्ति। अदृष्ट्वाऽपि तान्निरूप्य भयेन द्रष्टुस्तथा प्रतिभाति। तथा च गौतमखिलेषु -- दृष्ट्वा देवं मोदमाना अदृष्ट्वाऽप्येतद्भयाद्बिभ्यतो दृष्टवत्ते। पश्यन्ति ते न्यस्तचक्षुर्मुखांस्तु तस्मिन्नेवैते मनसो गतत्वात् इति।
commentaries.ramanujacharya:
।।द्युशब्दः पृथिवीशब्दश्च उभौ उपरितनानाम् अधस्तनानां च लोकानां प्रदर्शनार्थौ?
द्यावापृथिव्योः अन्तरम्
अवकाशः? यस्मिन् अवकाशे सर्वे लोकाः तिष्ठन्ति? सर्वः अयम् अवकाशः
दिशश्च सर्वाः त्वया एकेन
व्याप्ताः।
दृष्ट्वा
अद्भूतं रूपम्
उग्रं तव इदम्
अनन्तायामविस्तारम् अत्यद्भुतम्
अति उग्रं तव रूपं
दृष्ट्वा
लोकत्रयं प्रव्यथितम्
-- युद्धदिदृक्षया आगतेषु ब्रह्मादिदेवासुरपितृगणसिद्धगन्धर्वयक्षराक्षसेषु प्रतिकूलानुकूलमध्यस्थरूपं लोकत्रयं सर्वं प्रव्यथितम्? अत्यन्तभीतम्
महात्मन्
अपरिच्छेद्यमनोवृत्ते।ऐतेषाम् अपि अर्जुनस्य इव विश्वाश्रयरूपसाक्षात्कारसाधनं दिव्यं चक्षुः भगवता दत्तम्। किमर्थम् इति चेत् अर्जुनाय स्वैश्वर्यं सर्वं प्रदर्शयितुम् अत इदम् उच्यते -- दृष्ट्वाद्भुतं रूपमुग्रं तवेदं लोकत्रयं प्रव्यथितं महात्मन् इति।

shlokas.name: Shloka 21
shlokas.interpretation: This verse describes the cosmic form of Krishna as witnessed by Arjuna. It portrays the awe-inspiring and fearsome nature of the divine, emphasizing the different reactions of various celestial beings to this manifestation. Some approach with reverence, others with fear, while the great sages offer prayers. This shloka highlights the omnipotence of the Supreme Being and the varying levels of spiritual understanding among different entities.
shlokas.life_application: This verse teaches us to approach the divine with a balance of reverence and love. It reminds us that even in the face of overwhelming power or challenges, maintaining faith and offering our best efforts (like the prayers of the sages) is crucial. In daily life, this can translate to facing difficulties with courage, respecting authority without losing our dignity, and always striving for peace and harmony in our interactions with others and the world around us.

scripts.devanagari:
अमी हि त्वां सुरसङ्घा विशन्ति
केचिद्भीताः प्राञ्जलयो गृणन्ति।
स्वस्तीत्युक्त्वा महर्षिसिद्धसङ्घाः
स्तुवन्ति त्वां स्तुतिभिः पुष्कलाभिः

amī hi tvāṅ surasaṅghāḥ viśanti
kēcidbhītāḥ prāñjalayō gṛṇanti.
svastītyuktvā maharṣisiddhasaṅghāḥ
stuvanti tvāṅ stutibhiḥ puṣkalābhiḥ
scripts.kannada:
ಅಮೀ ಹಿ ತ್ವಾಂ ಸುರಸಙ್ಘಾಃ ವಿಶನ್ತಿ
ಕೇಚಿದ್ಭೀತಾಃ ಪ್ರಾಞ್ಜಲಯೋ ಗೃಣನ್ತಿ.
ಸ್ವಸ್ತೀತ್ಯುಕ್ತ್ವಾ ಮಹರ್ಷಿಸಿದ್ಧಸಙ್ಘಾಃ
ಸ್ತುವನ್ತಿ ತ್ವಾಂ ಸ್ತುತಿಭಿಃ ಪುಷ್ಕಲಾಭಿಃ

స్వస్తీత్యుక్త్వా మహర్షిసిద్ధసఙ్ఘాః
స్తువన్తి త్వాం స్తుతిభిః పుష్కలాభిః

translation.purohitSwami: The troops of celestial beings enter into Thee, some invoking Thee in fear, with folded palms; the Great Seers and Adepts sing hymns to Thy Glory, saying All Hail.'

commentaries.shankaracharya:
।। --,
अमी हि
युध्यमाना योद्धारः
त्वा
त्वां
सुरसंघाः
ये अत्र भूभारावताराय अवतीर्णाः वस्वादिदेवसंघाः मनुष्यसंस्थानाः त्वां
विशन्ति
प्रविशन्तः दृश्यन्ते। तत्र
केचित् भीताः प्राञ्जलयः
सन्तो
गृणन्ति
स्तुवन्ति त्वाम् अन्ये पलायनेऽपि अशक्ताः सन्तः। युद्धे प्रत्युपस्थिते उत्पातादिनिमित्तानि उपलक्ष्य
स्वस्ति
अस्तु जगतः
इति उक्त्त्वा महर्षिसिद्धसंघाः
महर्षीणां सिद्धानां च संघाः
स्तुवन्ति त्वां स्तुतिभिः पुष्कलाभिः
संपूर्णाभिः।।किं चान्यत् --,
commentaries.ramanujacharya:
।।
अमी सुरसंघाः उत्कृष्टाः त्वां
विश्वाश्रयम् अवलोक्य हृष्टमनसः त्वत्समीपं
विशन्ति।
तेषु एव
केचिद्
अति उग्रम् अति अद्भुतं च तव आकारम् आलोक्य
भीताः प्राञ्जलयः
स्वज्ञानानुगुणं स्तुतिरूपाणि वाक्यानि
गृणन्ति
उच्चारयन्ति। अपरे महर्षिसंघाः सिद्धसंघाः चपरावरतत्त्वयाथात्म्यविदः
स्वस्ति इति उक्त्वा पुष्कलाभिः
भगवदनुरूपाभिः
स्तुतिभिः स्तुवन्ति।

shlokas.meaning: The troops of celestial beings enter into Thee, some invoking Thee in fear, with folded palms; the Great Seers and Adepts sing hymns to Thy Glory, saying All Hail.'

shlokas.name: Shloka 22
shlokas.interpretation: This verse describes the awe-inspiring cosmic form of Lord Krishna, as witnessed by Arjuna. It emphasizes the universality and all-encompassing nature of the divine, showing how even celestial beings are amazed by this revelation. The verse illustrates the concept of God's omnipresence and the ultimate unity of all existence within the divine.
shlokas.life_application: This verse teaches us to recognize the divine presence in all aspects of existence, encouraging a broader perspective on life. It can help individuals overcome narrow-mindedness and prejudices by realizing the interconnectedness of all beings. In practical terms, this understanding can foster greater respect for diversity, promote environmental consciousness, and inspire a sense of wonder and humility in our daily lives.

shlokas.name: Shloka 23
shlokas.interpretation: This verse describes Arjuna's reaction to witnessing Krishna's cosmic form (Vishwaroop). It emphasizes the overwhelming and awe-inspiring nature of the divine manifestation, which is beyond human comprehension. The verse highlights the contrast between the limited human perception and the infinite, all-encompassing nature of the divine, inducing a sense of fear and reverence in the observer.
shlokas.life_application: This verse teaches us to recognize the vastness and complexity of the universe and our own limitations in understanding it. It encourages humility in the face of the unknown and respect for forces beyond our control. In daily life, this can be applied by approaching challenges with a sense of reverence, acknowledging that there may be aspects we don't fully comprehend, and remaining open to new perspectives and possibilities beyond our immediate understanding.

shlokas.name: Shloka 24

It emphasizes the overwhelming and awe-inspiring nature of the divine manifestation, which transcends human comprehension. The verse highlights the contrast between mortal limitations and divine infinitude, illustrating the profound impact of direct spiritual experience on the human psyche.
shlokas.life_application: This verse teaches us to approach the unknown and the vastness of existence with humility and reverence. It reminds us that there are aspects of reality that may be beyond our current understanding, encouraging open-mindedness and spiritual growth. In facing life's challenges, it suggests that moments of awe and realization can be transformative, pushing us beyond our comfort zones and inspiring personal evolution.

shlokas.name: Shloka 25
shlokas.interpretation: This verse describes Arjuna's reaction to witnessing Krishna's cosmic form (Vishwarupa). It emphasizes the overwhelming and terrifying nature of the divine manifestation, highlighting the contrast between human perception and the true nature of the divine. The verse also underscores the importance of divine grace and surrender in the face of the incomprehensible vastness of the universe.
shlokas.life_application: This verse teaches us to approach life's overwhelming challenges with humility and surrender. When faced with situations beyond our control or understanding, we should seek divine guidance and grace. It reminds us to cultivate a broader perspective on life, acknowledging our limitations and the vastness of the universe. This approach can help in managing stress, anxiety, and feelings of helplessness in difficult times.

shlokas.meaning: When I see Thy mouths with their fearful jaws like glowing fires at the dissolution of creation, I lose all sense of place; I find no rest. Be merciful, O Lord in whom this universe abides!

shlokas.name: Shloka 26
shlokas.interpretation: This verse describes Arjuna's vision of the Universal Form of Lord Krishna, where he sees all the warriors of both armies, including the sons of Dhritarashtra, kings, Bhishma, Drona, and Karna, along with the chief warriors of his own side, entering into Krishna's terrifying, all-consuming form. It symbolizes the inevitability of death and the ultimate power of the Divine, transcending human notions of friend and foe.
shlokas.life_application: This verse reminds us of the transient nature of life and the ultimate equality of all beings in the face of cosmic reality. It teaches us to transcend petty differences and conflicts, recognizing the divine presence in all. In practical life, this understanding can help us approach conflicts with a broader perspective, reduce ego-driven actions, and cultivate humility and compassion towards others, regardless of perceived differences or enmities.

shlokas.name: Shloka 27
shlokas.interpretation: This verse vividly describes the cosmic form of Lord Krishna, emphasizing its terrifying and all-consuming nature. It portrays the universal destruction at the end of time, symbolizing the cyclical nature of creation and destruction in Hindu philosophy. The imagery of beings rushing into the Lord's mouths represents the inevitability of death and the ultimate surrender of all existence to the Supreme Being.
shlokas.life_application: This verse reminds us of the transient nature of life and the ultimate power of the divine. It can help individuals face their fears, particularly the fear of death, by understanding that all beings are subject to the same cosmic laws. It encourages humility and surrender to a higher power, promoting a perspective that can reduce ego and attachment to worldly things. In facing life's challenges, one can draw strength from recognizing the larger cosmic order and one's place within it.

shlokas.name: Shloka 28
shlokas.interpretation: This verse draws a powerful analogy between rivers flowing into the ocean and warriors entering Krishna's cosmic form. It illustrates the inevitability of fate and the all-consuming nature of the divine. The image of warriors entering the blazing mouths symbolizes the ultimate dissolution of all beings into the supreme reality, emphasizing the transient nature of individual existence and the eternal nature of the divine.
shlokas.life_application: This verse can help individuals understand and accept the inevitability of change and death in life. It encourages embracing the natural flow of existence, letting go of attachments, and recognizing the larger cosmic order. In facing personal challenges or losses, one can find solace in understanding that all things eventually merge with the greater whole, just as rivers merge with the ocean.

shlokas.name: Shloka 29
shlokas.interpretation: This verse presents a powerful metaphor comparing the fate of all beings to moths drawn to a flame. It illustrates the cosmic form of Krishna as an all-consuming force, emphasizing the inevitability of death and the cyclical nature of existence. The imagery conveys the overwhelming power of the divine and the ultimate insignificance of individual beings in the face of cosmic reality.
shlokas.life_application: This verse can help individuals understand the transient nature of life and the importance of detachment. It encourages acceptance of life's impermanence, prompting us to focus on spiritual growth rather than material pursuits. In facing challenges, one can draw strength from recognizing the larger cosmic order, finding peace in surrendering to the flow of existence rather than resisting inevitable changes.

shlokas.name: Shloka 30
shlokas.interpretation: This verse vividly describes the cosmic form of Lord Krishna, emphasizing His all-encompassing and awe-inspiring nature. It portrays the Lord as consuming all worlds with His flaming mouths, symbolizing the cyclical nature of creation and destruction. The intense radiance emanating from His form represents the divine energy that permeates the entire universe, highlighting the omnipresence and omnipotence of the Supreme Being.
shlokas.life_application: This verse reminds us of the impermanence of worldly existence and the supreme power of the Divine. It encourages individuals to cultivate humility and surrender to a higher power, recognizing our limited role in the grand cosmic scheme. In facing life's challenges, one can draw strength from understanding that everything is part of a larger divine plan, helping to reduce ego and attachment to temporary situations.

shlokas.name: Shloka 31
shlokas.interpretation: This verse represents Arjuna's awe and confusion upon witnessing Krishna's cosmic form (Vishwaroop). It highlights the human struggle to comprehend the divine nature and emphasizes the importance of humility and surrender in the face of the supreme reality. The verse also underscores the limitations of human perception and understanding when confronted with the infinite and transcendental aspects of existence.
shlokas.life_application: This verse teaches us to approach life's mysteries and challenges with humility and an open mind. When faced with situations beyond our understanding, we should seek knowledge respectfully, acknowledging our limitations. It encourages us to cultivate curiosity and reverence for the unknown, which can lead to personal growth and spiritual development. In practical terms, this attitude can help in problem-solving, fostering better relationships, and maintaining mental peace in the face of life's complexities.

commentaries.madhvacharya: ।।धर्मान्तरज्ञानार्थमेव को भवानिति पृच्छति -- आख्याहीति। यथा कश्चित्कञ्चिन्नामादिकं जानन्नपि जातिज्ञानार्थं पृच्छति कस्त्वमिति। यदि त्वमेव न जानाति तर्हिविष्णो [11।30] इत्येव सम्बोधनं न स्यात्त्वमक्षरं [11।18] इत्यादि च।

अभिप्रेतां

एतद् आख्याहि मे नमोऽस्तु ते देववर प्रसीद -- नमः ते अस्तु सर्वेश्वर एवं कर्तुम् अनेन अभिप्रायेण इदं संहर्तृरूपम् आविष्कृतम् इति उक्त्वा प्रसन्नरूपश्च भव।आश्रितवात्सल्यातिरेकेण विश्वैश्वर्यं दर्शयतो भवतो घोररूपाविष्कारे कः अभिप्रायः इति पृष्टो भगवान् पार्थसारथिः स्वाभिप्रायम् आह -- पार्थोद्योगेन विना अपि धार्तराष्ट्रप्रमुखम् अशेषं राजलोकं निहन्तुम् अहम् एव प्रवृत्तः? इति ज्ञापनाय मम घोररूपाविष्कारः? तज्ज्ञापनं च पार्थम् उद्योजयितुम् इति --

shlokas.name: Shloka 32
shlokas.interpretation: This verse is a powerful declaration by Krishna, revealing his cosmic form as Time itself, the ultimate destroyer. It emphasizes the inevitability of fate and the supreme power of the Divine. Krishna asserts that he is the force that brings about the end of all worlds, and that the warriors on the battlefield are merely instruments in this grand cosmic plan. This revelation underscores the theme of divine will and the insignificance of individual actions in the face of cosmic destiny.
shlokas.life_application: This verse can help individuals understand the transient nature of life and the importance of detachment. It encourages acceptance of change and loss as natural parts of existence. In facing personal challenges or losses, one can find solace in recognizing the larger cosmic order at play. It also promotes humility by highlighting the limits of human agency in the face of greater forces, inspiring individuals to focus on their duties without being overly attached to outcomes.

commentaries.madhvacharya: ।।कालशब्दो जगद्बन्धनच्छेदनज्ञानादिसर्वभगवद्धर्मवाची। कल बन्धने? कल च्छेदने? कल ज्ञाने?,कल कामधेनुरिति पठन्ति। प्रसिद्धश्च स शब्दो भगवति।नियतं कालपाशेन बद्धं शक्र विकत्थसे। अयं स पुरुषः श्यामो लोकस्य हरति प्रजाः। बद्ध्वा तिष्ठति मां रौद्रः पशुं रशनया यथा इति मोक्षधर्मे। विष्णुना बद्धो बलिर्वक्तिविष्णौ चाधीश्वरे (त्र्यधीश्वरे) चित्तं धारयन् (येत्) कालविग्रहे [11।15।15] इति भागवते। प्रवृद्धः परिपूर्णोऽनादिर्वा। ऋतं च सत्यं चाभीद्धात् [ऋक्सं.8।8।49।1म.ना.6।1] इति हि श्रुतिः। एतत् (इदं) महद्भूतम् [बृ.उ.2।4।12] इति च।प्र विष्णुरस्तु तवसः स्तवीयांस्त्वेषं ह्यस्य स्थविरस्य नाम [ऋक्सं.5।6।25।3] इति च? न तु वर्धनम्।नासौ जजान न मरिष्यति नैधतेऽसौ इति हि भागवते।यस्य दिव्यं हि तद्रूपं हीयते वर्धते न च इति मोक्षधर्मे। न कर्मणा [बृ.उ.4।4।23] इति तु कर्मणाऽपि न? किमु स्वयं इति। लोकान्समाहर्तुमिह विशेषेण प्रवृत्तः। भ्रात्रादींश्च ऋते इत्यपिशब्दः। प्रत्यनीकत्वं तु परस्परतया। सर्वेऽपि न भविष्यन्ति? अक्षौहिण्यादिभेदेन बहुवचनं युक्तम्।

shlokas.name: Shloka 33
shlokas.interpretation: This verse encapsulates Krishna's call to action for Arjuna, emphasizing the concept of divine will and the role of humans as instruments of that will. It highlights the importance of fulfilling one's duty (dharma) without attachment to the outcome, as the results are predetermined by the divine. The verse also touches on the philosophical concept of free will versus determinism, suggesting a balance between human effort and divine plan.
shlokas.life_application: This verse can be applied in situations where one faces difficult decisions or challenging tasks. It encourages taking action without being paralyzed by fear of consequences. In professional life, it teaches to perform one's duties to the best of ability, leaving the results to a higher power. In personal struggles, it provides comfort by suggesting that larger forces are at play, and one's role is to act with integrity and without attachment to outcomes. This perspective can reduce stress and anxiety in decision-making processes and help maintain focus on present actions rather than worrying about future results.

shlokas.meaning: Then gird up thy loins and conquer. Subdue thy foes and enjoy the kingdom in prosperity. I have already doomed them. Be thou my instrument, Arjuna!

shlokas.name: Shloka 34
shlokas.interpretation: This verse represents Krishna's assurance to Arjuna about the predetermined outcome of the war. It emphasizes the concept of divine will and the role of individuals as instruments of that will. Krishna is reminding Arjuna that the warriors he's hesitant to fight are already slain by divine decree, and Arjuna's duty is to be the instrument of this divine plan without emotional attachment.
shlokas.life_application: This verse teaches us to perform our duties without fear or hesitation, understanding that larger forces are at play beyond our immediate perception. It encourages us to have faith in a higher power or purpose when facing challenging situations. In practical life, this can help in overcoming fear of failure, making difficult decisions, and maintaining composure in high-pressure situations by focusing on our actions rather than the outcomes.

shlokas.name: Shloka 35
shlokas.interpretation: This verse depicts Arjuna's reaction to witnessing Krishna's cosmic form. It illustrates the overwhelming nature of divine revelation and the humbling effect it has on even the most accomplished individuals. The verse emphasizes the importance of reverence and humility in the face of the divine, and how spiritual experiences can profoundly impact one's emotional and physical state.
shlokas.life_application: This verse teaches us to approach life's profound moments with humility and reverence. When faced with overwhelming situations or realizations, it's important to acknowledge our limitations and respond with respect and openness. This attitude can help us navigate challenging experiences, foster personal growth, and deepen our understanding of life's mysteries. It also reminds us to remain humble in the face of knowledge or power, recognizing that there is always something greater than ourselves.

shlokas.name: Shloka 36
shlokas.interpretation: This verse captures Arjuna's awe and reverence for Krishna's cosmic form. It emphasizes the universal impact of the divine manifestation, affecting all beings from the most exalted to the most fearsome. The verse illustrates the concept of bhakti (devotion) and the power of divine glory to inspire both love and fear.
shlokas.life_application: This verse teaches us about the power of divine presence in our lives. It encourages cultivating a sense of awe and respect for the supreme reality, which can lead to inner peace and spiritual growth. In practical terms, it reminds us to align ourselves with positive forces in life, to respect the power of goodness, and to understand that our actions have far-reaching consequences in the cosmic order.

commentaries.madhvacharya: ।।यदेतद्वक्ष्यमाणं तत्स्थाने युक्तमेवेत्यर्थः। अग्नीषोमाद्यन्तर्यामितया जगद्धर्षणादेर्हृषीकेशः? केशत्वं त्वंशूनां तन्नियतत्वादेः? प्रमाणं तुशशिसूर्यनेत्रं [11।19] इत्यत्रोक्तम्? हृषीकाणामिन्द्रियाणामीशत्वाच्च हृषीकेशः? तेषां विशेषतः ईशत्वं च यः प्राणे तिष्ठन् [बृ.उ.3।7।16] इत्यादौ प्रसिद्धम्।न मे हृषीकाणि पतन्त्यसत्पथे इत्यादिप्रयोगाच्च। इतरोऽर्थो मोक्षधर्मे सिद्धःसूर्याचन्द्रमसौ शश्वत्केशैर्मे अंशुसंज्ञितैः। बोधयन् स्थापयंश्चैव जगदुत्पद्यते पृथक्। बोधनात्स्थापनाच्चैव जगतो हर्षसम्भवात्। अग्नीषोमकृतैरेभिः कर्मभिः पाण्डुनन्दन। हृषीकेशो महेशानो वरदो लोकभावनः इति च।

shlokas.meaning: Arjuna said: My Lord! It is natural that the world revels and rejoices when it sings the praises of Thy glory; the demons fly in fear and the saints offer Thee their salutations.

shlokas.name: Shloka 37
shlokas.interpretation: This verse expresses Arjuna's awe and reverence for Krishna's cosmic form. It acknowledges Krishna as the supreme being, greater than even Brahma, the creator. The verse emphasizes the all-encompassing nature of Krishna, describing him as infinite, the lord of all gods, and the abode of the universe. It also touches on the philosophical concept of Krishna being both the manifest and unmanifest, transcending duality.
shlokas.life_application: This verse teaches us to recognize and revere the divine in all aspects of existence. It encourages humility and surrender to a higher power, which can help in overcoming ego and pride. Understanding our place in the vast cosmic order can provide perspective in dealing with life's challenges and promote a sense of interconnectedness with all beings. It also inspires us to look beyond surface-level differences and recognize the underlying unity in diversity.

shlokas.name: Shloka 38
shlokas.interpretation: This verse emphasizes the supreme nature of Krishna as the ultimate, all-encompassing divine being. It portrays Him as the primordial God, the eternal person, and the foundation of the entire universe. The verse also highlights Krishna's omniscience, describing Him as the knower of all that is to be known and the supreme abode. The concept of His infinite forms permeating the entire universe underscores the idea of divine immanence and transcendence simultaneously.
shlokas.life_application: This verse can help individuals develop a deeper understanding of the interconnectedness of all existence, fostering a sense of unity and respect for all life forms. It encourages seeking knowledge and wisdom, recognizing that the divine permeates everything. In practical terms, it can inspire people to approach life's challenges with humility, knowing that there is a higher power or cosmic order at play. This perspective can lead to reduced ego, increased compassion, and a more holistic approach to problem-solving in personal and professional life.

shlokas.name: Shloka 39
shlokas.interpretation: This verse is part of Arjuna's awe-struck reaction to witnessing Krishna's universal form. It emphasizes the all-encompassing nature of the Divine, equating Krishna with various cosmic forces and deities. The repetitive salutations underscore Arjuna's profound reverence and humility in the face of this overwhelming revelation.
shlokas.life_application: This verse teaches us to recognize the divine presence in all aspects of existence, fostering a sense of reverence for the world around us. It encourages humility by reminding us of our place within a vast, interconnected universe. In daily life, this perspective can help in developing respect for nature, practicing mindfulness, and approaching challenges with a broader, more spiritual outlook.

commentaries.madhvacharya: ।।11.37 -- 11.40।।कथं स्थाने इति तदाह -- कस्मादित्यादिना। पूर्णश्चासावात्मा चेति महात्मा। आत्मशब्दश्चोक्तो भारते -- यच्चाप्नोति यदादत्ते यच्चात्ति विषयानिह। यच्चास्य सन्ततो भावस्तस्मादात्मेति भण्यते इति। तत्परं सदसतः परम्।असच्च सच्चैव च यद्विश्वं सदसतः परम्। [म.भा.1।1।23] इति भारते।
commentaries.ramanujacharya:
।।सर्वेषां
प्रपितामहः

shlokas.meaning: Thou art the Wind, Thou art Death, Thou art the Fire, the Water, the Moon, the Father and the Grandfather. Honour and glory to Thee a thousand and a thousand times! Again and again, salutation be to Thee, O my Lord!

shlokas.name: Shloka 40
shlokas.interpretation: This verse expresses Arjuna's awe and reverence for Krishna's universal form. It acknowledges the omnipresence and omnipotence of the Divine, emphasizing that God pervades all directions and encompasses all of existence. The shloka highlights the infinite power and immeasurable prowess of the Supreme Being, reinforcing the concept of God's all-pervasiveness and ultimate reality.
shlokas.life_application: This verse teaches us to recognize the divine presence in all aspects of life, encouraging a perspective of reverence and humility. It can help individuals overcome ego and develop a sense of interconnectedness with all beings. In practical terms, this understanding can lead to greater respect for nature, improved interpersonal relationships, and a more holistic approach to problem-solving by considering the broader impact of our actions on the whole.

shlokas.name: Shloka 41
shlokas.interpretation: This verse represents Arjuna's realization and apology for his casual behavior towards Krishna before witnessing His divine form. It highlights the importance of recognizing the divine nature of the Supreme Being and the need for appropriate reverence. The verse also underscores the theme of human limitations in comprehending the true nature of the Divine.
shlokas.life_application: This verse teaches us to be mindful of our interactions with others, especially those we respect or who hold authority. It reminds us to avoid taking relationships for granted and to acknowledge our mistakes when we realize them. In professional settings, it encourages maintaining appropriate boundaries and respect, even in familiar relationships. Personally, it promotes self-reflection and the courage to apologize when we've acted inappropriately, fostering better interpersonal relationships and personal growth.

shlokas.name: Shloka 42
shlokas.interpretation: This verse represents the pinnacle of Arjuna's devotion and awe upon witnessing Krishna's cosmic form. It emphasizes the importance of complete surrender and reverence to the Divine. The repetitive use of 'namah' (salutations) signifies the overwhelming nature of the divine vision and Arjuna's inability to express his feelings adequately. It also illustrates the omnipresence of the Divine, as Arjuna offers salutations in all directions, recognizing God's all-pervasive nature.
shlokas.life_application: This verse teaches us the importance of humility and gratitude in our lives. It encourages us to recognize the divine in everything around us, fostering a sense of respect for all creation. In practical terms, this can translate to treating others with kindness and respect, regardless of their status or position. It also reminds us to approach life's challenges with a sense of reverence and acceptance, understanding that there's a greater purpose behind every experience. This attitude can help in reducing stress, improving relationships, and finding inner peace amidst life's complexities.

shlokas.name: Shloka 43
shlokas.interpretation: This verse represents Arjuna's realization of Krishna's supreme cosmic form. It acknowledges Krishna as the ultimate father, teacher, and most worshipable being in all of existence. The verse emphasizes the incomparable nature of Krishna's power and influence across all three worlds, highlighting the concept of God's omnipresence and supremacy in Hindu philosophy.
shlokas.life_application: This verse teaches us to recognize and respect the divine in all aspects of life. It encourages humility and devotion, reminding us that there is always a higher power guiding the universe. In practical terms, it can help individuals develop a sense of cosmic connection, reducing ego and promoting a more harmonious approach to relationships and challenges in life. It also emphasizes the importance of respecting teachers and elders, as they represent divine wisdom in human form.

shlokas.name: Shloka 44
shlokas.interpretation: This verse represents Arjuna's humble surrender to Krishna's cosmic form. It illustrates the complex relationship between the devotee and the divine, encompassing various aspects of human relationships like father-son, friend-friend, and lover-beloved. The verse emphasizes the importance of complete submission and seeking forgiveness, while also highlighting the multifaceted nature of the divine-human connection.
shlokas.life_application: This verse teaches us the importance of humility and seeking forgiveness in our relationships, both with the divine and with fellow humans. It encourages us to approach conflicts and misunderstandings with a spirit of reconciliation, recognizing that forgiveness is a divine quality. In professional settings, it reminds leaders to be compassionate and understanding, fostering an environment of trust and mutual respect. On a personal level, it inspires us to cultivate deeper, more meaningful relationships by being willing to admit our faults and seek reconciliation.

shlokas.name: Shloka 45
shlokas.interpretation: This verse captures Arjuna's complex emotional state upon witnessing Krishna's cosmic form. It illustrates the human response to the divine - a mixture of awe, joy, and fear. Arjuna's request to see Krishna's familiar form again demonstrates the human need for a relatable, comprehensible image of the divine, even after experiencing its vast, incomprehensible nature.
shlokas.life_application: This verse teaches us to balance our pursuit of spiritual growth with our human limitations. While seeking higher truths and experiences, we should also acknowledge our need for familiarity and comfort. It encourages us to approach the unknown with courage, but also reminds us that it's okay to seek reassurance and return to what we know when overwhelmed. In life, this can apply to personal growth, career changes, or any situation where we're pushing our boundaries - it's important to challenge ourselves, but also to know when to step back and regroup.

shlokas.name: Shloka 46
shlokas.interpretation: This verse marks a pivotal moment in Arjuna's experience of Krishna's cosmic form. Overwhelmed by the terrifying vision of the Universal Form, Arjuna expresses his desire to see Krishna in His familiar four-armed form. This request signifies Arjuna's preference for a more personal and relatable aspect of the Divine, highlighting the human tendency to seek comfort in the familiar even when faced with the ultimate reality.
shlokas.life_application: This verse teaches us about the importance of finding a balance between understanding the vastness of the universe and maintaining a personal connection with the divine. In life, we often face overwhelming situations that can make us feel small and insignificant. However, like Arjuna, we can seek comfort in a more relatable and personal aspect of our beliefs or values. This approach can help us navigate complex situations while maintaining our emotional and spiritual equilibrium.

shlokas.name: Shloka 47
shlokas.interpretation: This verse marks a pivotal moment in the Bhagavad Gita where Lord Krishna reveals His cosmic form to Arjuna. It emphasizes the special grace bestowed upon Arjuna and the uniqueness of this divine vision. The verse highlights the supreme nature of God's universal form, which is described as radiant, infinite, and primordial. It underscores the rarity and privilege of such a divine revelation, indicating that this vision is not accessible through ordinary means but only through God's grace and the power of yoga.
shlokas.life_application: This verse teaches us about the power of divine grace and the importance of spiritual practice. In life, we often seek profound experiences or insights. This shloka reminds us that true spiritual enlightenment comes not just from our efforts, but also through divine grace. It encourages us to cultivate a relationship with the divine through devotion and yoga, while remaining open to unexpected revelations. It also teaches humility, reminding us that there are aspects of reality beyond our normal perception, encouraging a sense of wonder and respect for the mysteries of existence.

shlokas.name: Shloka 48
shlokas.interpretation: This verse emphasizes the extraordinary nature of Krishna's cosmic form and the impossibility of perceiving it through conventional means. It highlights the supremacy of divine grace over human efforts in spiritual realization. The verse also underscores the unique position of Arjuna, who has been granted this vision not through his own merits but through Krishna's favor.
shlokas.life_application: This verse teaches us the importance of humility and surrender in spiritual pursuit. It reminds us that while personal efforts are necessary, ultimate spiritual realization comes through divine grace. In daily life, this principle can be applied by balancing hard work with faith, and by recognizing that some achievements are beyond our control and require a higher intervention. It encourages us to persist in our endeavors while remaining open to unexpected blessings and insights that transcend our limited understanding.

shlokas.name: Shloka 49
shlokas.interpretation: This verse marks a pivotal moment in the Bhagavad Gita where Krishna, having shown Arjuna His cosmic form, now comforts him. It illustrates the compassionate nature of the Divine, who recognizes the limitations of human perception and offers reassurance. The verse also emphasizes the importance of overcoming fear and confusion when faced with the overwhelming aspects of reality, encouraging a return to a state of love and devotion.
shlokas.life_application: This verse can be applied to situations where we face overwhelming challenges or truths that seem beyond our comprehension. It teaches us to approach life's difficulties with courage and faith, knowing that behind the apparent chaos and complexity, there is a benevolent force. In personal growth, it encourages us to confront our fears and limitations, trusting that we will emerge stronger and more enlightened. In leadership roles, it reminds us to be compassionate towards those who may be intimidated by change or new responsibilities, offering reassurance and guidance.

shlokas.name: Shloka 50
shlokas.interpretation: This verse marks a pivotal moment in the Bhagavad Gita, where Krishna transitions from his cosmic form back to his familiar human-like appearance. It highlights the compassionate nature of the Divine, who recognizes and responds to the devotee's emotional state. The verse also underscores the concept of divine grace, as Krishna willingly reveals and conceals his true nature to guide Arjuna's spiritual journey.
shlokas.life_application: This verse teaches us about the importance of adapting our approach when guiding or leading others. Just as Krishna shifted his form to comfort Arjuna, we too should be sensitive to others' emotional states and adjust our communication style accordingly. It also reminds us that in times of fear or uncertainty, we can find solace in familiar and comforting presences, whether spiritual or personal. Furthermore, it encourages us to balance awe-inspiring experiences with gentleness and compassion in our interactions with others.

shlokas.name: Shloka 51
shlokas.interpretation: This verse marks a significant moment in Arjuna's spiritual journey. After witnessing Krishna's cosmic form, Arjuna is relieved to see Krishna return to his gentle human form. This transition symbolizes the accessibility of the divine, showing that while God's universal form is awe-inspiring, His personal form is what allows for intimate connection and devotion. It also highlights the importance of balance between understanding God's supremacy and relating to Him personally.
shlokas.life_application: This verse teaches us about managing overwhelming experiences and finding balance. In life, we may encounter situations that shake us to our core, much like Arjuna's vision of the cosmic form. The lesson here is to seek and appreciate the familiar and comforting aspects of our spiritual practice or relationships to regain our composure. It encourages us to cultivate a personal, intimate connection with the divine or our higher principles, which can serve as an anchor during turbulent times. This approach can help in stress management, dealing with existential crises, and maintaining emotional stability in the face of life's profound experiences.

shlokas.meaning: Arjuna said: Seeing Thee in Thy gentle human form, my Lord, I am myself again, calm once more.

shlokas.name: Shloka 52
shlokas.interpretation: This verse emphasizes the rarity and significance of Arjuna's divine vision. Lord Krishna reveals that even the gods constantly yearn to witness this cosmic form, highlighting the exceptional nature of Arjuna's experience. It underscores the profound spiritual privilege granted to Arjuna and the immense grace of the Divine in revealing its true nature to a devoted seeker.
shlokas.life_application: This verse encourages us to cultivate deep devotion and spiritual practices, as they can lead to profound spiritual experiences. It teaches us to appreciate rare spiritual insights when they occur and to remain humble in our spiritual journey. In daily life, it reminds us to seek and value the extraordinary in the ordinary, to be open to moments of divine revelation in our everyday experiences, and to persist in our spiritual endeavors despite challenges.

translation.purohitSwami: Lord Shri Krishna replied: It is hard to see this vision of Me that thou hast seen. Even the most powerful have longed for it in vain.

shlokas.name: Shloka 53
shlokas.interpretation: This verse emphasizes the supremacy of divine grace over ritualistic practices or intellectual pursuits in attaining a vision of God's cosmic form. Krishna states that the magnificent form Arjuna has witnessed cannot be seen through conventional means of spiritual practice or knowledge acquisition. It underscores the importance of devotion and divine favor in experiencing the highest spiritual truths.
shlokas.life_application: This verse teaches us that while spiritual practices and knowledge are important, they are not sufficient for the highest spiritual realizations. It encourages us to cultivate sincere devotion and surrender to the divine, reminding us that in our spiritual journey, grace plays a crucial role. In practical life, this can be applied by balancing our efforts with faith, humility, and openness to divine guidance, rather than relying solely on our own abilities or rigid practices.

shlokas.meaning: Not by study of the scriptures, or by austerities, not by gifts or sacrifices, is it possible to see Me as thou hast done.

shlokas.name: Shloka 54
shlokas.interpretation: This verse emphasizes the supreme importance of unwavering devotion (bhakti) in realizing the Divine. Krishna reveals that only through single-minded devotion can one truly understand, see, and enter into His cosmic form. It highlights the power of bhakti as a means to transcend the limitations of human perception and intellect, enabling a direct, experiential understanding of the Divine.
shlokas.life_application: This verse teaches us the importance of dedication and single-minded focus in achieving our goals. In our personal and professional lives, we can apply this principle by cultivating unwavering commitment to our chosen path. Whether it's in relationships, career, or personal growth, maintaining steadfast devotion and eliminating distractions can lead to deeper understanding, clearer vision, and ultimate success in our endeavors.

shlokas.meaning: Only by tireless devotion can I be seen and known; only thus can a man become one with Me, O Arjuna!

shlokas.name: Shloka 55
shlokas.interpretation: This verse encapsulates the essence of devotion and the path to attain Krishna. It outlines the qualities of a true devotee who can reach the Divine. The verse emphasizes the importance of selfless action, devotion, detachment, and universal love as key elements in spiritual progress. It suggests that by embodying these qualities, one can transcend the material world and unite with the Supreme.
shlokas.life_application: This verse can be applied in daily life by encouraging individuals to perform their duties with a sense of devotion, viewing work as worship. It teaches the importance of maintaining equanimity and avoiding hatred or resentment towards others. By cultivating detachment from the fruits of one's actions and fostering universal love, one can lead a more peaceful and spiritually fulfilling life. This approach can help in managing stress, improving relationships, and finding purpose in one's actions.

chapters.name: Bhakti Yoga
chapters.summary: Chapter 12 of the Bhagavad Gita focuses on Bhakti Yoga, the path of devotional service to God. Krishna explains the superiority of devotional service over other forms of spiritual practice and describes the qualities of an ideal devotee.

chapters.philosophical_progression: The chapter begins with a comparison between personal devotion and impersonal worship, establishing the superiority of Bhakti Yoga. It then progresses to describe alternative paths for those who find steady devotion challenging, emphasizing the importance of dedicating all actions to the Divine. The latter part of the chapter focuses on describing the qualities of an ideal devotee, emphasizing equanimity, detachment, and unwavering faith.
chapters.chapter_relevance: Chapter 12 is crucial in establishing Bhakti Yoga as a superior and more accessible path to spiritual realization. It provides practical guidance for devotees at different levels of spiritual advancement and emphasizes the importance of cultivating divine qualities. This chapter serves as a bridge between the more philosophical discussions in earlier chapters and the practical aspects of devotional service, making it highly relevant for those seeking a balance between knowledge and devotion in their spiritual practice.

shlokas.name: Shloka 1
shlokas.interpretation: This verse marks the beginning of Chapter 12, where Arjuna seeks clarification on the superior form of worship. He asks Krishna to compare those who worship Him with devotion and those who meditate on the formless, impersonal Absolute. This question reflects the eternal debate in Hindu philosophy between saguna (with attributes) and nirguna (without attributes) worship, and sets the stage for Krishna's explanation of different paths to spiritual realization.
shlokas.life_application: This verse encourages individuals to reflect on their own spiritual inclinations and preferences. It validates different approaches to spirituality, whether through devotion to a personal God or meditation on the formless Absolute. This understanding can help people respect diverse spiritual practices, reduce religious conflicts, and choose a path that resonates with their nature and temperament for effective spiritual growth.

commentaries.madhvacharya: ।।उपासनाप्रियाय नमः। । अव्यक्तोपासनाद्भगवदुपासनस्योत्तमत्वं प्रदर्श्य तदुपायं प्रदर्शयत्यस्मिन्नध्याये तदुपासनमपि मोक्षसाधनं प्रतीयते श्रियं वसाना अमृतत्वमायन्भवन्ति सत्या समिथा मितद्रौ [ऋक्सं.7।4।4।4] इति। अनाद्यनन्तं महतः परं ध्रुवं निचाय्य तन्मृत्युमुखात्प्रमुच्यते [कठो.3।15] इति च। अव्यक्तं च महतः परम्। महतः परमव्यक्तम् [कठो.3।11] इत्युक्तपरामर्शोपपत्तेः।उपास्य तां श्रियमव्यक्तसंज्ञां भक्त्या मर्त्यो मुच्यते सर्वबन्धैः इति सामवेदे आग्निवेश्यशाखायाम्। महच्च माहात्म्यं तस्या वेदेषूच्यते -- चतुष्कपर्दा युवतिः सुपेशा घृतप्रतीका वयुनानि वस्ते। तस्यां सुपर्णा वृषणा निषेदतुर्यत्र देवा दधिरे भागधेयम्। [ऋक्सं.8।6।16।3] चतुःशिखण्डा युवतिः सुपेशा घृतप्रतीका वयुनानि वस्ते इति च।अहं रुद्रेभिर्वसुभिश्चराम्यहमादित्यैरुत विश्वदेवैः इत्यारभ्य अहं राष्ट्री सङ्गमनी वसूनां चिकितुषी प्रथमा यज्ञियानाम्। तां मा देवा व्यदधुः पुरुत्रा भूरिस्थात्रां भूर्यावेशयन्तीम्। मया सो अन्नमत्ति यो विपश्यति यः प्राणिति य ईं श्रृणोत्युक्तम्। अमन्तवो मां त उपक्षियन्ति श्रुधि श्रुत श्रद्धिवं ते वदामि। यं कामये तं तमुग्रं कृणोमि तं ब्रह्माणं तमृषिं तं सुमेधाम्। अहं रुद्राय धनुरातनोमि ब्रह्मद्विषे शरवे हन्तवा उ।।अहं सुवे पितरमस्य मूर्धन्मम योनिरप्स्वान्तस्समुद्रे। परो दिवा पर एना पृथिव्यै तावती महिना सम्बभूव [ऋक्सं.8।7व.11?12] इत्यादि च। त्वया जुष्ट ऋषिर्भवति देवि त्वया ब्रह्म गतश्रीरुत त्वया [म.ना.13।2] इति च। इति शङ्का कस्यचिद्भवति? अतो जानन्नपि सूक्ष्मयुक्तिज्ञानार्थं पृच्छति -- एवमिति। एवंशब्देन दृष्टश्रुतरूपंमत्कर्मकृत् [11।55] इत्यादिप्रकारश्च परामृश्यते।अव्यक्तं प्रकृतिः।महतः परमव्यक्तं [कठो.3।12] इति प्रयोगात्।यत्तत् त्रिगुणमव्यक्तं नित्यं सदसदात्मकम्।प्रधानं प्रकृतिं प्राहुरविशेषं विशेषवत् [3।26।10] इति च भागवते। अक्षरं च तत्। अक्षरात्परतः परः [मु.उ.2।1।2] इति श्रुतेः। परं तु ब्रह्म न हि भगवतोऽन्यत्।आनन्दमानन्दमयेऽवसाने सर्वात्मके ब्रह्मणि वासुदेवे [   ] इति भागवते। रूपं चेदृशं साधितं पुरस्तात्। उपासनं च तथैव कार्यम्। सहस्रशीर्षा पुरुषः सहस्राक्षः सहस्रपात् [ऋक्सं.8।4।17।1श्वे.उ.3।14] इत्यारभ्य तमेवं विद्वानमृत इह भवति [नृ.पू.ता.1।6] नान्यः पन्था अयनाय विद्यते [श्वे.उ.3।8] इति साम्यासा।आदित्यवर्णत्वादिश्च न वृथोपचारत्वेनाङ्गीकार्यः। तथा च सामवेदे सौकरायणश्रुतिः -- स्थाणुर्ह वै प्राजापत्यः स प्रजापतिं पितरमेत्योवाच। मुमुक्षुभिः साधुभिः पूतपापैः किमु ह वै तारकं तारवाच्यम्। ध्यानं च तस्याप्तरुचेः कथं स्याद्ध्येयश्च कः पुरुषोऽलोमपादः इति। तं होवाचैष वै विष्णुस्तारकोऽलोमपादो ध्यानं च तस्याप्तरुचेर्वदामि। सोऽनन्तशीर्षो बहुवर्णः सुवर्णो ध्येयः स वै लोहितादित्यवर्णः। श्यामोऽथ वा हृदये सोऽष्टबाहुरनन्तवीर्योऽनन्तबलः पुराणः इति। अरूपत्वा देस्तु गतिरुक्ता। पुरुषभेदश्च प्रश्नादौ प्रतीयते। त्वां पर्युपासतेये चाप्यक्षरमव्यक्तं इत्यादौ।

shlokas.name: Shloka 2
shlokas.interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of unwavering devotion and constant focus on the Divine. It suggests that the highest form of spiritual practice involves completely immersing one's mind in the Supreme Being. The Lord considers those who worship Him with steadfast faith and perpetual concentration as the most perfectly united with Him. This verse establishes a hierarchy in spiritual practices, placing those who are constantly absorbed in thoughts of the Divine at the pinnacle.
shlokas.life_application: This verse can be applied in daily life by encouraging individuals to cultivate a focused and devoted mindset in their spiritual practices. It teaches the importance of consistency and faith in one's chosen path. In a broader sense, it can inspire people to approach their goals and responsibilities with unwavering dedication and concentration, leading to excellence in any field. The teaching also emphasizes the power of faith and positive thinking in overcoming life's challenges and achieving personal growth.

श्री भगवानुवाच
मय्यावेश्य मनो ये मां नित्ययुक्ता उपासते।
श्रद्धया परयोपेतास्ते मे युक्ततमा मताः
shlokas.transliteration:
śrī bhagavānuvāca
mayyāvēśya manō yē māṅ nityayuktā upāsatē.
śraddhayā parayōpētāstē mē yuktatamā matāḥ
shlokas.meaning: Lord Shri Krishna replied: Those who keep their minds fixed on Me, who worship Me always with unwavering faith and concentration; these are the very best.

shlokas.name: Shloka 3
shlokas.interpretation: This verse describes the nature of the Absolute Truth or Brahman and the devotees who worship It. It emphasizes the transcendental, imperceptible, and all-pervading nature of the Supreme. The verse also highlights the steadfast devotion of those who focus on this formless aspect of the Divine, suggesting that such worship requires great spiritual maturity and abstract thinking.
shlokas.life_application: This verse encourages individuals to cultivate a broader, more inclusive perspective of reality beyond the material world. It can help in developing detachment from temporary situations, reducing anxiety about change, and fostering a sense of inner peace by connecting with the unchanging, eternal aspect of existence. Practically, it can be applied in meditation practices, stress management, and developing a more philosophical approach to life's challenges.

shlokas.name: Shloka 4
shlokas.interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of self-control, equanimity, and universal compassion in spiritual practice. It suggests that those who can restrain their senses, maintain a balanced perspective in all situations, and dedicate themselves to the welfare of all beings are the ones who truly attain the Divine. This teaching aligns with the broader Gita philosophy of detached action and seeing the Divine in all creation.
shlokas.life_application: This verse can be applied in daily life by practicing mindfulness and self-control in our actions and reactions. By cultivating a balanced perspective in both positive and negative situations, we can reduce stress and make better decisions. Engaging in acts of kindness and considering the well-being of others in our choices can lead to a more fulfilling and harmonious life. This approach can help in resolving conflicts, improving relationships, and finding inner peace amidst life's challenges.

संनियम्येन्द्रियग्रामं सर्वत्र समबुद्धयः।
ते प्राप्नुवन्ति मामेव सर्वभूतहिते रताः
shlokas.transliteration:
saṅniyamyēndriyagrāmaṅ sarvatra samabuddhayaḥ.
tē prāpnuvanti māmēva sarvabhūtahitē ratāḥ
shlokas.meaning: Subduing their senses, viewing all conditions of life with the same eye, and working for the welfare of all beings, assuredly they come to Me.

shlokas.name: Shloka 5
shlokas.interpretation: This verse highlights the challenges faced by those who are attached to the unmanifested, impersonal aspect of the Divine. It suggests that the path of devotion to the formless is more difficult for embodied beings, as it is harder to concentrate on something without form or attributes. The verse implies that for most people, especially those with strong bodily consciousness, it is easier to worship and connect with a personal form of God.
shlokas.life_application: This verse can help individuals choose a spiritual path that aligns with their nature and capabilities. For those struggling with abstract concepts in meditation or spiritual practice, it suggests that adopting a more personal approach to divinity, such as devotional practices or visualization techniques, might be more effective and less stressful. It encourages practitioners to be honest about their spiritual inclinations and choose methods that resonate with their current level of understanding and bodily awareness.

अतः क्लेशः अधिकतरः।।अक्षरोपासकानां यत् वर्तनम्? तत् उपरिष्टाद्वक्ष्यामः --,
commentaries.madhvacharya: ।।कथं तर्हि त्वदुपासकानामुत्तमत्वं इत्यत आह -- क्लेश इति। अव्यक्ता गतिर्दुःखं ह्यवाप्यते। गतिर्मार्गः। अव्यक्तोपासनद्वारको मत्प्राप्तिमार्गो दुःखमवाप्यत इत्यर्थः। अतिशयोपासनसर्वेन्द्रियातिनियमनसर्वसमबुद्धिसर्वभूतहितेरतत्वातिसुष्ट्वाचारसम्यग्विष्णुभक्त्यादिसाधनसन्दर्भमृते नाव्यक्तापरोक्षम्।तदृते च न विष्णुप्रसादः। सत्यपि तस्मिन्नसम्यग्भगवदुपासनमृते नर्ते च तं मोक्षः? विनाऽव्यक्तोपासनं भवत्येव भगवदुपासकानां मोक्ष इति क्लेशिष्ठो़ऽयं मार्ग इति भावः। तथाप्यपरोक्षीकृताव्यक्तानां सुकरं भगवदुपासनमित्येव प्रयोजनम्। तत्रापि योऽव्यक्तापरोक्षे प्रयासस्तावता प्रयासेन यदि भगवन्तमुपास्ते? ऊनेन वा? तदा भगवदपरोक्षमेव भवतीति द्वितीयमधिकम्। इन्द्रियसंयमाद्यूनभावे अत्युपासकस्यापि देवी नातिप्रसादमेति। देवस्तु तानि साधनानि भक्तिमतः स्वयमेव प्रयत्नेन ददातीति सौकर्यमिति भक्तानां भगवुपासने। इतरत्र च क्लेशोऽधिकतरः।तदेतत्सर्वं पर्युपासते सन्नियम्याधिकतर इति परिसन्तरप्शब्दैः प्रतीयते। सामवेदे माधुच्छन्दशाखायां चोक्तम् -- भक्ताश्च येऽतीव विष्णावतीव जितेन्द्रियाः सम्यगाचारयुक्ताः। उपासते तां समबुद्धयश्च तेषां देवी दृश्यते नेतरेषाम्। दृष्टा च सा भक्तिमतीव विष्णौ दत्त्वोपास्ते सर्वविघ्नांश्छिनत्ति। उपास्य तं वासुदेवं विदित्वा ततस्ततः शान्तिमत्यन्तमेति इति। उक्तं च सामवेदे अयास्यशाखायाम् -- प्रसन्नो भविता देवः सोऽव्यक्तेन सहैव तु। यावता तत्प्रसादो हि तावतैव न संशयः। न तत्प्रसादमात्रेण प्रीयते स महेश्वरः। तस्मिन्प्रीते तु सर्वस्य प्रीतिस्त भवति ध्रुवम्।।यद्यप्युपासनाधिक्यं तथापि गुणदो हि सः। मुक्तिदश्च स एवैको नाव्यक्तादिस्तु कश्चन इति।ममात्मभावमिच्छन्तो यतन्ते परमात्मने [म.भा.12।228।20] इति मोक्षधर्मे श्रीवचनम्।धर्मनित्ये महाबुद्धौ ब्रह्मण्ये सत्यवादिनि। प्रश्रिते दानशीले च सदैव निवसाम्यहम् [म.भा.12।228।26] इति च।महतः परं तु ब्रह्मैव। तथा हि भगवता सयुक्तिकमभिहितम्।वदतीति चेन्न प्राज्ञो हि  त्रयाणामेव चैवमुपन्यासः प्रश्नश्चेत्यादि। तमिति पुल्लिङ्गाच्चैतत्सिद्धिः। महतः परत्वं तु अव्यक्तपरस्य भवत्येव। तथा चाग्निवेश्यशाखायाम् -- अनाद्यनन्तं महतः परं ध्रुवम् [कठो.3।15] इति। परो हि देवः पुरुहूतो महत्तः इति। न चाव्यक्तरूपं भगवता निषिद्धं भारतादौ साधितत्वात्। शरीररूपकविन्यस्तगृहीतेरित्यादौ तु साङ्ख्यप्रसिद्धं,प्रधानं निषिध्य वैदिकमव्यक्तमेवोक्तम्। तथा च सौकरायणश्रुतिः -- शरीररूपिका अशरीरस्य विष्णोर्यतः प्रिया सा जगतः प्रसूतिः इति। सुव्रतानां क्षिप्रं महदैश्वर्यं ददाति देवी न देव इति विशेषः। सुवर्णवर्णां पद्मकरां च देवीं सर्वेश्वरीं व्याप्तजडां च बुद्ध्वा। सैवेति वै सुव्रतानां तु मासान्महाविभूतिं श्रीस्तु दद्यान्न देवः इत्यृग्वेदखिलेषु।

shlokas.name: Shloka 6
shlokas.interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of complete surrender and devotion to the Divine. It describes the highest form of devotees who dedicate all their actions to God and meditate on Him with unwavering focus. This represents the path of Bhakti Yoga, where the devotee's entire existence is centered around the Divine, free from any other attachments or distractions.
shlokas.life_application: This teaching can be applied in daily life by encouraging individuals to perform their duties with a sense of devotion and selflessness. By dedicating our actions to a higher purpose, we can find greater meaning and fulfillment in our work and relationships. It also emphasizes the importance of maintaining focus and concentration in our pursuits, whether spiritual or worldly, to achieve excellence and inner peace.

shlokas.name: Shloka 7
shlokas.interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine promise of liberation for those who are fully devoted to Krishna. It illustrates the concept of divine grace and the power of bhakti (devotion) in overcoming the cycle of birth and death. The metaphor of the 'ocean of death and rebirth' (samsara) highlights the spiritual struggles faced by individuals, while Krishna's assurance of swift rescue underscores the efficacy of surrender and devotion in spiritual practice.
shlokas.life_application: This verse can be applied to overcome feelings of hopelessness or being trapped in difficult life situations. It encourages focusing one's mind on a higher purpose or divine ideal to find strength and guidance. In practical terms, it suggests that by cultivating devotion and maintaining unwavering focus on one's spiritual goals, one can overcome life's challenges more easily and find peace amidst turmoil. It also teaches the importance of faith and perseverance in achieving long-term goals, whether spiritual or material.

मत्प्राप्तिविरोधितया मृत्युभूतान्
संसारा
ख्यात्
सागराद् अहम्
अचिरेण एव कालेन

shlokas.meaning: O Arjuna! I rescue them from the ocean of life and death, for their minds are fixed on Me.

shlokas.name: Shloka 8
shlokas.interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of complete surrender and devotion to the Divine. Krishna instructs Arjuna to fix his mind and intellect solely on Him, assuring that by doing so, one will undoubtedly dwell in the Divine consciousness. It highlights the path of Bhakti Yoga, where the devotee's entire being is focused on God, leading to ultimate union and liberation.
shlokas.life_application: This teaching can be applied in daily life to overcome distractions and achieve focus. By centering one's thoughts and actions on a higher purpose or goal, individuals can find clarity, reduce anxiety, and make more meaningful progress in their personal and professional lives. It encourages developing a single-pointed concentration, which can enhance productivity, decision-making, and overall well-being.

shlokas.name: Shloka 9
shlokas.interpretation: This verse addresses the situation where a devotee finds it challenging to maintain unwavering focus on the Divine. Krishna advises Arjuna that if he cannot achieve steady meditation, he should engage in abhyasa yoga, which is the practice of repeatedly bringing the mind back to God. This verse emphasizes the importance of persistent effort and practice in spiritual growth, acknowledging that not everyone can immediately achieve perfect concentration.
shlokas.life_application: This teaching can be applied to various aspects of life where consistent practice is key to improvement. Whether in learning a new skill, overcoming bad habits, or developing a positive mindset, the principle of repeated effort (abhyasa) is crucial. It encourages individuals not to give up when faced with difficulties but to keep trying. In meditation or mindfulness practices, it reminds us that it's normal for the mind to wander and that the practice lies in gently bringing it back to focus repeatedly.

shlokas.meaning: But if thou canst not fix thy mind firmly on Me, then, My beloved friend, try to do so by constant practice.

shlokas.name: Shloka 10
shlokas.interpretation: This verse offers a compassionate alternative for those who find meditation and constant remembrance of God challenging. It emphasizes the importance of dedicating one's actions to the Divine, suggesting that even routine work, when performed with the right attitude, can lead to spiritual progress. This teaching aligns with the concept of Karma Yoga, where one's duties become a means of worship and self-realization.
shlokas.life_application: This verse can be applied in daily life by encouraging individuals to infuse their regular activities with a sense of higher purpose. It offers solace to those who struggle with traditional spiritual practices, showing that one's profession, household duties, or any form of work can become a spiritual path when performed with the right mindset. This approach can reduce stress, increase job satisfaction, and provide a sense of meaning in seemingly mundane tasks.

translation.purohitSwami: And if thou are not strong enough to practise concentration, then devote thyself to My service, do all thine acts for My sake, and thou shalt still attain the goal.

shlokas.name: Shloka 11
shlokas.interpretation: This verse addresses those who find it challenging to practice constant meditation or devotion. It offers a practical alternative, suggesting that if one cannot fully engage in yoga or devotional practices, they should at least perform their duties without attachment to the results. This teaching emphasizes the importance of selfless action and detachment from outcomes, which are fundamental principles of Karma Yoga.
shlokas.life_application: This verse can be applied in daily life by encouraging individuals to focus on their responsibilities and perform their duties to the best of their abilities, without being overly concerned about the results. It teaches us to work with dedication and sincerity, letting go of anxiety about outcomes. This approach can reduce stress, improve work quality, and foster a sense of inner peace and contentment in various aspects of life, including career, relationships, and personal growth.

ततः

।।अथ मद्योगम् आश्रित्य
एतद् अपि कर्तुं
न शक्नोषि? मद्गुणानुसंधानकृतं मदेकप्रियत्वाकारं भक्तियोगम् आश्रित्य भक्तियोगाङ्गरूपम् एतद् मत्कर्म अपि कर्तुं न शक्नोषि

shlokas.transliteration:

shlokas.meaning: And if thou art too weak even for this, then seek refuge in union with Me, and with perfect self-control renounce the fruit of thy action.

shlokas.name: Shloka 12
shlokas.interpretation: This verse presents a hierarchy of spiritual practices, emphasizing the progressive nature of spiritual evolution. It suggests that knowledge is superior to practice, meditation is superior to knowledge, and renunciation of the fruits of action is superior to meditation. Ultimately, it points to peace as the final outcome of this spiritual progression, indicating that true peace comes from detachment and selfless action.
shlokas.life_application: This verse can be applied in daily life by encouraging individuals to move beyond rote learning or mechanical practices and seek deeper understanding. It promotes the practice of mindfulness and meditation to gain clarity and inner peace. Most importantly, it teaches the value of performing actions without attachment to results, which can reduce stress, anxiety, and disappointment in personal and professional life. By focusing on the action itself rather than its outcome, one can find greater satisfaction and peace in their endeavors.

6।14) इति सर्वकामप्रहाणात् अमृतत्वम् उक्तम् तत् प्रसिद्धम्। कामाश्च सर्वे श्रौतस्मार्तकर्मणां फलानि। तत्त्यागे च विदुषः ध्याननिष्ठस्य अनन्तरैव शान्तिः इति सर्वकामत्यागसामान्यम् अज्ञकर्मफलत्यागस्य अस्ति इति तत्सामान्यात् सर्वकर्मफलत्यागस्तुतिः इयं प्ररोचनार्था। यथा अगस्त्येन ब्राह्मणेन समुद्रः पीतः इति इदानींतनाः अपि ब्राह्मणाः ब्राह्मणत्वसामान्यात् स्तूयन्ते? एवं कर्मफलत्यागात् कर्मयोगस्य श्रेयःसाधनत्वमभिहितम्।।
अत्र च आत्मेश्वरभेदमाश्रित्य विश्वरूपे ईश्वरे चेतःसमाधानलक्षणः योगः उक्तः? ईश्वरार्थं कर्मानुष्ठानादि च। अथैतदप्यशक्तोऽसि (गीता 12।11) इति अज्ञानकार्यसूचनात् न अभेददर्शिनः अक्षरोपासकस्य कर्मयोगः उपपद्यते इति दर्शयति तथा कर्मयोगिनः अक्षरोपासनानुपपत्तिम्। ते प्राप्नुवन्ति मामेव (गीता 12।4) इति अक्षरोपासकानां कैवल्यप्राप्तौ स्वातन्त्र्यम् उक्त्वा? इतरेषां पारतन्त्र्यात् ईश्वराधीनतां दर्शितवान् तेषामहं समुद्धर्ता (गीता 12।7) इति। यदि हि ईश्रवस्य आत्मभूताः ते मताः अभेददर्शित्वात्? अक्षरस्वरूपाः एव ते इति समुद्धरणकर्मवचनं तान् प्रति अपेशलं स्यात्। यस्माच्च अर्जुनस्य अत्यन्तमेव हितैषी भगवान् तस्य सम्यग्दर्शनानन्वितं कर्मयोगं भेददृष्टिमन्तमेव उपदिशति। न च आत्मानम् ईश्वरं प्रमाणतः बुद्ध्वा कस्यचित् गुणभावं जिगमिषति कश्चित्? विरोधात्। तस्मात् अक्षरोपासकानां सम्यग्दर्शननिष्ठानां संन्यासिनां त्यक्तसर्वैषणानाम् अद्वेष्टा सर्वभूतानाम् (गीता 12।13) इत्यादिधर्मपूतं साक्षात् अमृतत्वकारणं वक्ष्यामीति प्रवर्तते --
commentaries.madhvacharya: ।।अज्ञानपूर्वादभ्यासाज्ज्ञानमेव विशिष्यते। ज्ञानमात्रात्सज्ञानं ध्यानम्। तथा च सामवेदे अनभिम्लानशाखायाम् -- अधिकं केवलाभ्यासाज्ज्ञानं तत्सहितं ततः। ध्यानं ततश्चापरोक्षं ततः शान्तिर्भविष्यति इति। ध्यानात्कर्मफलत्यागः इति तु स्तुतिः। अन्यथा कथमसमर्थोऽसीत्युच्यतेतयोस्तु कर्मसन्न्यासात्कर्मयोगो विशिष्यते [5।2] इति चोक्तम्। सर्वाधिकं ध्यानमुदाहरन्ति ध्यानाधिके ज्ञानभक्ती परात्मन्। कर्माफलाकाङ्क्षमथो विरागस्त्यागश्च न ज्ञानकलाफलार्हाश्च इति च काषायणशाखायाम्।वाक्यसाम्येऽप्यसमर्थविषयत्वोक्तेस्तात्पर्याभाव इतरत्र प्रतीयते। ध्यानादिप्राप्तिकारणत्वाच्च त्यागस्तुतिर्युक्ता। केवलध्यानात्फलत्यागयुक्तं ध्यानमधिकम्। ध्यानयुक्तत्याग एव चात्रोक्तः। अन्यथा कथंत्यागाच्छान्तिरनन्तरं इत्युच्यते कथं च ध्यानादाधिक्यम् तथा च गौपवनशाखायाम् -- ध्यानात्तु केवलात्त्यागयुक्तं तदधिकं भवेत् इति। न हि त्यागमात्रानन्तरमेव मुक्तिर्भवति भवति च ध्यानयुक्तात्। केवलत्यागस्तुतिरेवमपि भवति। यथाऽनेन युक्तो जेता? नान्यथेत्युक्तेः।

dhyānātkarmaphalatyāgastyāgācchāntiranantaram
shlokas.meaning: Knowledge is superior to blind action, meditation to mere knowledge, renunciation of the fruit of action to meditation, and where there is renunciation peace will follow.

shlokas.name: Shloka 13
shlokas.interpretation: This verse describes the qualities of a true devotee of the Divine. It emphasizes the importance of cultivating universal love, compassion, and equanimity. The verse suggests that spiritual advancement is characterized by freedom from hatred, ego, and attachment, as well as the ability to remain balanced in both joy and sorrow. These attributes are essential for one who wishes to progress on the spiritual path and attain union with the Divine.
shlokas.life_application: This verse can be applied to cultivate better relationships and inner peace. By practicing non-hatred and friendliness towards all, one can reduce conflicts and stress in daily life. Developing compassion helps in understanding others' perspectives, leading to more harmonious interactions. Letting go of possessiveness and ego can lead to reduced anxiety and a more fulfilling life. Maintaining equanimity in both good and bad times helps in staying balanced and resilient. Forgiveness allows one to let go of grudges, promoting mental well-being and healthier relationships.

shlokas.name: Shloka 14
shlokas.interpretation: This verse describes the qualities of a devotee who is dear to Krishna. It emphasizes the importance of contentment, self-control, firm determination, and complete surrender of mind and intellect to the Divine. The verse highlights that true devotion is not just about rituals or external practices, but about one's inner state and attitude towards life and the Divine.
shlokas.life_application: This verse teaches us to cultivate contentment in all situations, practice self-discipline, develop unwavering determination in our spiritual pursuits, and surrender our thoughts and intellect to a higher purpose. These qualities can help us maintain peace of mind in challenging times, make better decisions, and lead a more fulfilling life. By focusing on inner growth rather than external circumstances, we can find true happiness and spiritual progress.

मय्यर्पितमनोबुद्धिर्यो मद्भक्तः स मे प्रियः
shlokas.transliteration:
santuṣṭaḥ satataṅ yōgī yatātmā dṛḍhaniścayaḥ.
mayyarpitamanōbuddhiryō madbhaktaḥ sa mē priyaḥ
shlokas.meaning: Always contented, self-centred, self-controlled, resolute, with mind and reason dedicated to Me, such a devotee of Mine is My beloved.

shlokas.name: Shloka 15
shlokas.interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of equanimity and emotional stability in spiritual life. It describes a person who neither disturbs others nor is disturbed by them, maintaining inner peace regardless of external circumstances. Such individuals have transcended the common emotional reactions of joy, anger, fear, and anxiety, which often control people's behavior. Lord Krishna expresses his fondness for such balanced individuals, indicating that this state of being is highly desirable on the spiritual path.
shlokas.life_application: This teaching can be applied in daily life to maintain emotional balance in challenging situations. By cultivating a non-reactive mindset, one can navigate personal and professional relationships more effectively, make better decisions under pressure, and experience less stress. Practicing mindfulness and developing a broader perspective on life's events can help achieve this state of equanimity. In conflict resolution, this approach can lead to more harmonious outcomes as one learns to respond thoughtfully rather than react impulsively to provocations or disappointments.

scripts.devanagari:

हर्षामर्षभयोद्वेगैर्मुक्तो यः स च मे प्रियः

translation.purohitSwami: He who does not harm the world, and whom the world cannot harm, who is not carried away by any impulse of joy, anger or fear, such a one is My beloved.

commentaries.shankaracharya:
।। --,

संन्यासिनः
न उद्विजते

तथा

न

shlokas.name: Shloka 16
shlokas.interpretation: This verse describes the qualities of a devotee who is dear to Krishna. It emphasizes detachment, purity, efficiency, impartiality, freedom from anxiety, and renunciation of selfish initiatives. These attributes collectively represent a state of spiritual maturity and complete surrender to the divine, highlighting the importance of inner transformation in the path of devotion.
shlokas.life_application: This verse guides us to cultivate detachment from outcomes, maintain mental and physical purity, develop skills to serve efficiently, remain impartial in conflicts, overcome anxiety through faith, and renounce selfish actions. By embodying these qualities, one can achieve peace of mind, improve relationships, enhance work performance, and progress spiritually. It encourages a life of purpose beyond personal gain, fostering a sense of inner fulfillment and harmony with the divine will.

scripts.devanagari:
अनपेक्षः शुचिर्दक्ष उदासीनो गतव्यथः।
सर्वारम्भपरित्यागी यो मद्भक्तः स मे प्रियः
scripts.roman:
anapēkṣaḥ śucirdakṣa udāsīnō gatavyathaḥ.
sarvārambhaparityāgī yō madbhaktaḥ sa mē priyaḥ

translation.purohitSwami: He who expects nothing, who is pure, watchful, indifferent, unruffled, and who renounces all initiative, such a one is My beloved.

commentaries.shankaracharya:
।। --,देहेन्द्रियविषयसंबन्धादिषु अपेक्षाविषयेषु
अनपेक्षः
निःस्पृहः।
शुचिः
बाह्येन आभ्यन्तरेण च शौचेन संपन्नः।
दक्षः
प्रत्युत्पन्नेषु कार्येषु सद्यः यथावत् प्रतिपत्तुं समर्थः।
उदासीनः
न कस्यचित् मित्रादेः पक्षं भजते यः? सः उदासीनः यतिः।
गतव्यथः
गतभयः।
सर्वारम्भपरित्यागी
आरभ्यन्त इति आरम्भाः इहामुत्रफलभोगार्थानि कामहेतूनि कर्माणि सर्वारम्भाः? तान् परित्यक्तुं शीलम् अस्येति सर्वारम्भपरित्यागी
यः मद्भक्तः सः मे प्रियः
।।किञ्च --,
commentaries.madhvacharya: ।।सर्वारम्भपरित्यागी इत्यादेः सामान्यविशेषव्याख्यानव्याख्येयभावेनापुनरुक्तिः। हर्षादिभिर्मुक्त इत्युक्ते कादाचित्कमपि भवतीतियो न हृष्यति [12।17] इत्युक्तम्। उपचारपरिहारार्थं पूर्वम् आधिक्यज्ञानार्थं भक्त्यभ्यासः।ये तु सर्वाणि कर्माणि [12।6] इत्यादेः प्रपञ्च एषः।
commentaries.ramanujacharya:
।।
अनपेक्षः
-- आत्मव्यतिरिक्ते कृत्स्ने वस्तुनि अनपेक्षः?
शुचिः
-- शास्त्रविहितद्रव्यवर्धितकायः?
दक्षः
-- शास्त्रीयक्रियोपादानसमर्थः अन्यत्र
उदासीनः? गतव्यथः
-- शास्त्रीयक्रियानिर्वृत्तौ अवर्जनीयशीतोष्णपरुषस्पर्शादिदुःखेषु व्यथारहितः? सर्वारम्भपरित्यागी -- शास्त्रीयव्यतिरिक्तसर्वकर्मारम्भपरित्यागी? य एवंभूतो मद्भक्तः स मे प्रियः।

shlokas.transliteration:

shlokas.meaning: He who expects nothing, who is pure, watchful, indifferent, unruffled, and who renounces all initiative, such a one is My beloved.

shlokas.name: Shloka 17
shlokas.interpretation: This verse describes the qualities of a devotee who is dear to Krishna. It emphasizes the importance of equanimity, detachment, and unwavering devotion. The ideal devotee remains unaffected by the dualities of life, neither elated by positive experiences nor dejected by negative ones. This state of mind reflects a deep understanding of the transient nature of worldly experiences and a firm grounding in spiritual wisdom.
shlokas.life_application: This verse teaches us to cultivate emotional balance and detachment in our daily lives. By not getting overly excited about successes or depressed about failures, we can maintain mental peace and focus on our spiritual growth. It encourages us to let go of our attachments to outcomes, both good and bad, and instead focus on performing our duties with devotion. This approach can help reduce stress, anxiety, and disappointment, leading to a more fulfilling and peaceful life.

तथाविधम् अप्राप्तं च न

पापवत् पुण्यस्य अपि बन्धहेतुत्वाविशेषाद् उभयपरित्यागी?
यः
एवंभूतो

shlokas.name: Shloka 18
shlokas.interpretation: This verse describes the qualities of an ideal devotee who has transcended duality and attachment. It emphasizes the importance of equanimity in all situations, whether facing friends or foes, honor or dishonor, pleasure or pain. The verse highlights the spiritual maturity required to remain unaffected by external circumstances and maintain inner balance.
shlokas.life_application: This teaching can be applied in daily life to maintain emotional stability and mental peace. By cultivating equanimity, one can better handle workplace conflicts, personal relationships, and life's ups and downs. It encourages developing a non-reactive mindset, which leads to better decision-making and reduced stress. Practicing detachment from outcomes while performing one's duties can lead to increased focus and effectiveness in professional and personal endeavors.

shlokas.name: Shloka 19
shlokas.interpretation: This verse describes the qualities of a devotee who is dear to Krishna. It emphasizes equanimity, contentment, and steadfastness in devotion. The ideal devotee remains unaffected by praise or criticism, maintains inner silence, finds satisfaction in whatever comes their way, is detached from material possessions, and has unwavering faith. These attributes reflect a state of spiritual maturity and complete surrender to the divine.
shlokas.life_application: This verse teaches us to cultivate emotional balance and inner peace in our daily lives. By remaining unaffected by others' opinions, practicing contentment, and focusing on spiritual growth rather than material possessions, we can reduce stress and anxiety. It encourages us to develop resilience in the face of life's ups and downs, maintain a clear and focused mind, and find fulfillment through devotion and spiritual practices rather than external circumstances.

shlokas.interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of devotion and faith in spiritual practice. Krishna declares that those who follow the path of righteousness with unwavering faith and devotion are exceptionally dear to him. It highlights the significance of not just knowing the dharma, but living it fully with complete surrender to the Divine.

It teaches that by combining righteous living with devotion, one can find favor with the Divine and achieve inner peace. In daily life, this can be applied by maintaining integrity in one's actions, nurturing faith during challenging times, and dedicating one's work and efforts to a higher purpose, leading to a more fulfilling and purposeful existence.
